Examples of patterns could include that it is usually cooler in the morning than in the afternoon and the number of sunny days versus cloudy days in different months.

1BDE9C80DFE60131615068A86D17958E.description: Cite examples that demonstrate how the natural agents of wind , water, and ice produce slow changes on the Earth's surface such as carving out deep canyons and building up sand dunes.

1BDE2DF0DFE60131614F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the natural force of gravity causes changes in Earth's surface features as it pulls things toward Earth, as in mud and rock slides, avalanches, etc.

1BDDD720DFE60131614E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe events such as tornadoes, hurricanes, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, and flooding which change surface features rapidly.

1BDD8630DFE60131614D68A86D17958E.description: Cite and describe the processes that cause rapid or slow changes in Earth's surface.

1BDD3E10DFE60131614C68A86D17958E.description: Materials and Processes That Shape A Planet

1BDCF130DFE60131614B68A86D17958E.description: Earth/Space Science - Students will use scientific skills and processes to explain the chemical and physical interactions (i.e., natural forces and cycles, transfer of energy) of the environment, Earth, and the universe that occur over time.

1BDC8990DFE60131614A68A86D17958E.description: Realize that one way to make sense of something is to think how it is like something more familiar.

1BDC1860DFE60131614968A86D17958E.description: Explain that models, such as geometric figures, number sequences, graphs, diagrams, sketches, number lines, maps, and stories can be used to represent objects, events, and processes in the real world, although such representations can never be exact in every detail.

1BDBD080DFE60131614868A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that seeing how a model works after changes are made to it may suggest how the real thing would work if the same were done to it.

1BDB83B0DFE60131614768A86D17958E.description: Explain that a model is a simplified imitation of something and that a model's value lies in suggesting how the thing modeled works.

1BDB3BC0DFE60131614668A86D17958E.description: Examine and modify models and discuss their limitations.

1BDAF380DFE60131614568A86D17958E.description: Explain that something may not work as well (or at all) if a part of it is missing, broken, worn out, mismatched, or misconnected.

1BDAAA30DFE60131614468A86D17958E.description: Realize that in something that consists of many parts, the parts usually influence one another.

1BDA51C0DFE60131614368A86D17958E.description: Investigate a variety of mechanical systems and analyze the relationship among the parts.

1BDA09C0DFE60131614268A86D17958E.description: Identify factors that must be considered in any technological design—cost, safety, environmental impact, and what will happen if the solution fails.

1BD9BFA0DFE60131614168A86D17958E.description: Realize that there is no perfect design and that usually some features have to be sacrificed to get others, for example, designs that are best in one respect (safety or ease of use) may be inferior in other ways (cost or appearance).

1BD96F20DFE60131614068A86D17958E.description: Choose appropriate common materials for making simple mechanical constructions and repairing things.

1BD91510DFE60131613F68A86D17958E.description: Develop designs and analyze the products: "Does it work?" "Could I make it work better?" "Could I have used better materials?"

1BD85800DFE60131613D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that doing science involves many different kinds of work and engages men and women of all ages and backgrounds.

1BD810C0DFE60131613C68A86D17958E.description: Construct and share reasonable explanations for questions asked.

1BD7C7A0DFE60131613B68A86D17958E.description: Submit work to the critique of others which involves discussing findings, posing questions, and challenging statements to clarify ideas.

1BD77C70DFE60131613A68A86D17958E.description: Avoid choosing and reporting only the data that show what is expected by the person doing the choosing.

1BD73100DFE60131613968A86D17958E.description: Make use of and analyze models, such as tables and graphs to summarize and interpret data.

1BD6CC10DFE60131613868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that clear communication is an essential part of doing science because it enables scientists to inform others about their work, expose their ideas to criticism by other scientists, and stay informed about scientific discoveries around the world.

1BD626F0DFE60131613668A86D17958E.description: Keep a notebook that describes observations made, carefully distinguishes actual observations from ideas and speculations about what was observed, and is understandable weeks or months later.

1BD5DF30DFE60131613568A86D17958E.description: Review different explanations for the same set of observations and make more observations to resolve the differences.

1BD596F0DFE60131613468A86D17958E.description: Offer reasons for their findings and consider reasons suggested by others.

1BD54AC0DFE60131613368A86D17958E.description: Develop explanations using knowledge possessed and evidence from observations, reliable print resources, and investigations.

1BD4FD60DFE60131613268A86D17958E.description: Seek better reasons for believing something than "Everybody knows that…" or "I just know" and discount such reasons when given by others.

1BD46860DFE60131613068A86D17958E.description:
Judge whether measurements and computations of quantities are reasonable in a familiar context by comparing them to typical values when measured to the nearest:
  • Millimeter - length
  • Square centimeter - area
  • Milliliter - volume
  • Newton - weight
  • Gram - mass
  • Second - time
  • Degree C - temperature

1BD42360DFE60131612F68A86D17958E.description: Identify possible reasons for differences in results from investigations including unexpected differences in the methods used or in the circumstances in which the investigation is carried out, and sometimes just because of uncertainties in observations.

1BD3DDF0DFE60131612E68A86D17958E.description: Follow directions carefully and keep accurate records of one's work in order to compare data gathered.

1BD39540DFE60131612D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the results of scientific investigations are seldom exactly the same, and when the differences are large, it is important to try to figure out why.

1BD34840DFE60131612C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that comparisons of data might not be fair because some conditions are not kept the same.

1BD2EFC0DFE60131612B68A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate tools hand lens or microscope (magnifiers), centimeter ruler (length), spring scale (weight), balance (mass), Celsius thermometer (temperature), graduated cylinder (liquid volume), and stopwatch (elapsed time) to augment observations of objects, events, and processes.

1BD2A700DFE60131612A68A86D17958E.description: Support investigative findings with data found in books, articles, and databases, and identify the sources used and expect others to do the same.

1BD25980DFE60131612968A86D17958E.description: Gather and question data from many different forms of scientific investigations which include reviewing appropriate print resources, observing what things are like or what is happening somewhere, collecting specimens for analysis, and doing experiments.

1BD17060DFE60131612768A86D17958E.description: Skills and Processes - Students will demonstrate the thinking and acting inherent in the practice of science.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Mathematics (PK-8)

4210B08E71B64858849290CDE810078D.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D5748A196381474B9F308F6DA93825EC.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers. Examples: Express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6; locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

9C818591707448D1853D71500E33BA53.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

852EB7AF44ED40DE8BC83F46A416EB12.description: Represent two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on the number line.

0E1342ED9E914102A85F51952F3F5FF0.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

D50B7FE50EBD45C381E2EC39B05142C3.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

61EED8B7C4604E4F840AFBE64D7D10FA.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

094446A7D9B946E7A7BD52F6146C4FB4.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

09342ACCA1074FEB84CFF5D7BC17E921.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as ¼ of the area of the shape.

A2603C2E949C4EF1B6A24B506401F83B.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

ED8759B142064AF5BF1E8BB6801460D6.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes

D41AB531ADC54B8EADCC5707AC791544.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

0294D7E1CEA04E308670EC8C3CEDE08D.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

E565DCB031514BC8AB4E612883618AA9.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

CDFFB3A00D8C43739E0DD7DAEB96D9AD.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a x b and a x c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

199E67A140F6482A898F73FDC10DF76B.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

644D565BE7C74D6A8560CB2B5B236E95.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

072FA8DE11B142C4B1DD02548C63F1A1.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

B3024D2D78D94DE280F55F59AEAAA70B.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in., square ft., and improvised units).

A7881E9450C7444A87B0DF06CC1F762B.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

BAA1EDB814AA4986A7B2EB13F94098F0.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

F714013D30DE4337A35D486A27311CC8.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concept of area measurement.

178B490156D64DAF82A934494E12D134.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

A3F5B82E282647FBA0CAA24907A7806E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units – whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

FDDB2C7BA2C04489A64E8B017000A8AB.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how may less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs. For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

9E0F601963E146D79C6A167C8790E391.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

C5971755C7AE413682284ADF5A0C4D8A.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

C9B5FEEC49F44216AE97FE086B314D4C.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects

C308C681AAF94444989B4534F8764CF7.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range of 10-90 (e.g., 9 x 80, 5 x 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

9F022763A9CB44349747B8F127B92F6C.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

DB80AC77C53E4041840105D70D9F7813.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

044A03E98C114FA28DBE5C316AA954BB.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

32200833D4594773A7F4BB5A020A085B.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

9D8053685C6E450ABA3EC21E50527E4E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations. For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

9914BC17137D4603A44034C811C3005E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

374ED329182E49DCACD24CDBC9BCB7FD.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

0F90DD8A8385430C9A49B35224C70AD7.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 x 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

4B7EDD52D5BB4A3797E5A76C6706B4B7.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem. For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

DA9D25AC29584C46A6C5C68418C6B7A4.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
  • If 6 x 4 = 24 is known, then 4 x 6 = 24 is also known. (Commutative property of multiplication)
  • 3 x 5 x 2 can be found by 3 x 5 = 15, then 15 x 2 = 30, or by 5 x 2 = 10, then 3 x 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication)
  • Knowing that 8 x 5 = 40 and 8 x 2 = 16, one can find 8 x 7 as 8 x (5 + 2) = (8 x 5) + (8 x 2) which leads to 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property)

633012B88E6B4A488EC0C309B0AEAC86.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division

3FF545E653A54D289A70C3EC1AD654EC.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 x ? = 48, 5 =☐ ÷ 3, 6 x 6 = ?

7B5779F2111749C4BEB61514F16B189B.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

2814FBCC9C9948308C3F866601CC66EF.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each. For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷8.

12896AC5EF2B4875BBF99F54F7FF5BF1.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 x 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each. For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 x 7.

6A5340CE03C7478495ED628F5DB49F3F.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

BA6525EE51474F6A9EA529C3D592612A.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

F0139E250BE54A058681E27997579679.description: Look for and make use of structure.

4AEC5CFF3A40412CAD031933B7BF628B.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

96C65B03F5D44444A6F12F323C6F3AB7.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

1B837880DFE60131607268A86D17958E.description: Realize that one way to make sense of something is to think how it is like something more familiar.

1B832160DFE60131607168A86D17958E.description: Explain that models, such as geometric figures, number sequences, graphs, diagrams, sketches, number lines, maps, and stories can be used to represent objects, events, and processes in the real world, although such representations can never be exact in every detail.

1B82C5B0DFE60131607068A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe that seeing how a model works after changes are made to it may suggest how the real thing would work if the same were done to it.

1B827D40DFE60131606F68A86D17958E.description: Explain that a model is a simplified imitation of something and that a model's value lies in suggesting how the thing modeled works.

1B8232A0DFE60131606E68A86D17958E.description: Examine and modify models and discuss their limitations.

1B81DCF0DFE60131606D68A86D17958E.description: Explain that something may not work as well (or at all) if a part of it is missing, broken, worn out, mismatched, or misconnected.

1B818C50DFE60131606C68A86D17958E.description: Realize that in something that consists of many parts, the parts usually influence one another.

1B814610DFE60131606B68A86D17958E.description: Investigate a variety of mechanical systems and analyze the relationship among the parts.

1B80FE00DFE60131606A68A86D17958E.description: Identify factors that must be considered in any technological design—cost, safety, environmental impact, and what will happen if the solution fails.

1B80B5C0DFE60131606968A86D17958E.description: Realize that there is no perfect design and that usually some features have to be sacrificed to get others, for example, designs that are best in one respect (safety or ease of use) may be inferior in other ways (cost or appearance).

1B806B10DFE60131606868A86D17958E.description: Choose appropriate common materials for making simple mechanical constructions and repairing things.

1B8013A0DFE60131606768A86D17958E.description: Develop designs and analyze the products: "Does it work?" "Could I make it work better?" "Could I have used better materials?"

1B7F65B0DFE60131606568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that doing science involves many different kinds of work and engages men and women of all ages and backgrounds.

1B7F2140DFE60131606468A86D17958E.description: Construct and share reasonable explanations for questions asked.

1B7ED920DFE60131606368A86D17958E.description: Submit work to the critique of others which involves discussing findings, posing questions, and challenging statements to clarify ideas.

1B7E8F30DFE60131606268A86D17958E.description: Avoid choosing and reporting only the data that show what is expected by the person doing the choosing.

1B7E4290DFE60131606168A86D17958E.description: Make use of and analyze models, such as tables and graphs to summarize and interpret data.

1B7DCDE0DFE60131606068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that clear communication is an essential part of doing science because it enables scientists to inform others about their work, expose their ideas to criticism by other scientists, and stay informed about scientific discoveries around the world.

1B7D3E80DFE60131605E68A86D17958E.description: Keep a notebook that describes observations made, carefully distinguishes actual observations from ideas and speculations about what was observed, and is understandable weeks or months later.

1B7CF380DFE60131605D68A86D17958E.description: Review different explanations for the same set of observations and make more observations to resolve the differences.

1B7CAAF0DFE60131605C68A86D17958E.description: Offer reasons for their findings and consider reasons suggested by others.

1B7C6180DFE60131605B68A86D17958E.description: Develop explanations using knowledge possessed and evidence from observations, reliable print resources, and investigations.

1B7C0A00DFE60131605A68A86D17958E.description: Seek better reasons for believing something than "Everybody knows that…" or "I just know" and discount such reasons when given by others.

1B7B7520DFE60131605868A86D17958E.description:
Judge whether measurements and computations of quantities are reasonable in a familiar context by comparing them to typical values when measured to the nearest:
  • Millimeter - length
  • Square centimeter - area
  • Milliliter - volume
  • Newton - weight
  • Gram - mass
  • Second - time
  • Degree C - temperature

1B7B2890DFE60131605768A86D17958E.description: Identify possible reasons for differences in results from investigations including unexpected differences in the methods used or in the circumstances in which the investigation is carried out, and sometimes just because of uncertainties in observations.

1B7AD840DFE60131605668A86D17958E.description: Follow directions carefully and keep accurate records of one's work in order to compare data gathered.

1B7A70F0DFE60131605568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the results of scientific investigations are seldom exactly the same, and when the differences are large, it is important to try to figure out why.

1B7A08E0DFE60131605468A86D17958E.description: Explain that comparisons of data might not be fair because some conditions are not kept the same.

1B79C510DFE60131605368A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate tools hand lens or microscope (magnifiers), centimeter ruler (length), spring scale (weight), balance (mass), Celsius thermometer (temperature), graduated cylinder (liquid volume), and stopwatch (elapsed time) to augment observations of objects, events, and processes.

1B797F90DFE60131605268A86D17958E.description: Support investigative findings with data found in books, articles, and databases, and identify the sources used and expect others to do the same.

1B793730DFE60131605168A86D17958E.description: Gather and question data from many different forms of scientific investigations which include reviewing appropriate print resources, observing what things are like or what is happening somewhere, collecting specimens for analysis, and doing experiments.

1B789D60DFE60131604F68A86D17958E.description: Skills and Processes - Students will demonstrate the thinking and acting inherent in the practice of science.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Mathematics (PK-8)

3CC303352E9A4A47975FDE7B0B66E5E2.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

5A0F4D5A6BB3424AAC0CE9D51AFA3E06.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 and 100. For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

112448D6FF54442B84E9AB0408D4187F.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100. For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

0153F6F2668C494BBB6006188FD4D515.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

51543AFC1E924CEF931602B715A069FD.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, if a person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

43F046DD1DA242858681C7FD52A90F48.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number. For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 x (2/5) as 6 x (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n x (a/b) = (n x a)/b.)

6FEB6515E0C34599AF8633BE1888C394.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b. For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product of 5 x (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 x (1/4).

99016FAB34DE4151BE35152521D5363F.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

BA1B106CE2ED4541A2C9A063D78F0689.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

9DF37BF026DD4440ACBB8CDF935FAD69.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

B97FD4653532415C8246408775DC63CD.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition as an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model. Examples: 3/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8; 3/8 = 1/8 + 2/8; 2 1/8 = 1 + 1+ 1/8; 2 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8.

793998F78452433EB8ACE0E573F169B9.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole

3D573E190CB84FD78CE7DD5572BF6317.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b

66B2CFE134324B1AA71FD0DCCAD6EEC5.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

25F0492AB4794A918138BCE56DCCBD56.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

843A2F9799924C0E9101C6A5E893EA5D.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n x a)/(n x b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

BA971C135E8B41F2839CB594266517BE.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

677C0B8FB5D8414E9465E961E98990BD.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

48C279B61CBD40A4AB37113FAD7C9D1E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

FB599E1A14C54DF7B46676A12A410948.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

F600D3B2B9DE4A3991FBE523058FA5A1.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

E7D79E78752B4FEC893FF9B7411CE6E4.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

887FA938FE7C4E2DB26DB0CEBA8D0BE7.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

83088391FC484E60876A18B327EA99DB.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

502D7656D9B14B46B717170820AF4341.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of the circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

445516A6991E481988BA2CCFDD5896CA.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.

D254184EA1E7493089092976A44E5222.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

D6435267298F480A925E104C9FC424D7.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots. For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

D8A43F0D49DC43558105A565B3350C06.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems. For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formulas as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

478FBDADFE9648DBB86E2283BCEAE7FD.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

05F50FF1237345D89B89FD6FC69DECC3.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm, kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table. For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), 3, 36), …

ECFFF1409A6F4F388910632C2B2FFCB4.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements for a larger unit to a smaller unit.

E44C51E9BE564252B5AEE90E6B54353F.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

C4C0FABE976547DC9A2962FA62A4A8B8.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

C946668877D74D73A65BF933BE70E608.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

E2946C9A9D07456BBCBC9A325DD110FA.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

AA0072D0E4E14490AF9FD975A311CCCC.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

311B7CDC83CE410D9156AD8233D5AFFB.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

D3AEC90DF6704C70AB7BD0869B625295.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represent in the place to its right. For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

384B774B635D4030B269752EEB628A46.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

2B11EC9B391841CB9AD0962CB76B920E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

B66215912F9842199F7ADA148DE0BA96.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

86ABD60C1C7D4C6888B8777C635A8B1F.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range of 1-100 is prime or composite.

8C0809F8015442E6B270C5C01446BB92.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

0226A284C4CA4AF19A3CA6837C59A7C3.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

6522F8B71A1C43F4A8208512821E492D.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

5F2813016AF946DDAC110B22D6691596.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 x 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

7824361D591340A09A4C5D60CB2C3926.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

ED0849F9C56941399F618C9955D9FDB5.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

76E2B8B25F1B4ABAA5909732E579BBDB.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BBD509E7871C46779E54411F13743078.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

6A0430FA7ABB41DB947F9D9F30C8AE0E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - English Language Arts

B6111FBB2A0E4A269C3F296B084AEC06.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

45238A4574B541C18012610AEE066E2C.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

47FFF4D316CB48B4BA270FBE50A48560.description: Analyze grade 8 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced").

23DDFF2A4E694A2C8AD26F2C9E85ACFA.description: Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new").

A72EC4AA575E4FD3968264D404DD7F4C.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

AC0A33E7A54943A3922E007F41C2B555.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

AC09C5B4ADCE45D395AE649D0C1B5C30.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; using search terms effectively; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

8986A3CFC1BA41F2814908681DA05685.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

993364EACD4342EFB6535287C32C9A38.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

D3357665C5B7402A80ABAB13718E6FFE.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

60E102F029754D868806F4D7E940ECE0.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

2000D5F8173141B7871FCA39FDD69480.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

1AA80860DFE601315F0368A86D17958E.description: Analyze dramatic works to identify dramatic action

1AA7C0B0DFE601315F0268A86D17958E.description: Identify, analyze, and apply criteria to assess dramatic works and other literature of the theatre

1AA77EB0DFE601315F0168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how artistic choices observed in exemplary professional theatrical performances convey meaning

1AA73B40DFE601315F0068A86D17958E.description: Explain how artistic choices communicate meaning in individual and ensemble performances

1AA6A4A0DFE601315EFE68A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply criteria to analyze individual and group theatre processes

1AA667E0DFE601315EFD68A86D17958E.description: Aesthetics and Criticism: Students will demonstrate the ability to make aesthetic judgments.

1AA5E830DFE601315EFB68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which scenic elements and props might solve dramatic problems and create multiple uses for them that demonstrate the application of creative behaviors, such as fluency, originality, flexibility, and elaboration

1AA5A920DFE601315EFA68A86D17958E.description: Use collaborative theatre processes to create, perform, and revise scenes and plays

1AA56A50DFE601315EF968A86D17958E.description: Use selected posture, movement, expression, and vocal skills to create characters

1AA526C0DFE601315EF868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of theatre performance and production skills in formal and informal presentations

1AA4D1E0DFE601315EF768A86D17958E.description: Manipulate formal elements of performance, including time and space, to create improvisational scenes based on original or given ideas

1AA48870DFE601315EF668A86D17958E.description: Use dramatic narrative conventions to improvise scenes from books, short stories, or folktales

1AA43960DFE601315EF568A86D17958E.description: Create a text for performance using narrative conventions and dialogue to retell folktales and short stories

1AA3ECB0DFE601315EF468A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of theatrical elements to communicate ideas and feelings

1AA33620DFE601315EF268A86D17958E.description: Interpret the form and content of dramatic works expressively by using readers' theatre techniques

1AA2ECC0DFE601315EF168A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which playwrights use personal experience, imagination, history, literature, and heritage as creative resources

1AA2AC80DFE601315EF068A86D17958E.description: Develop knowledge of dramatic works by reading, performing, and attending selected plays

1AA26C10DFE601315EEF68A86D17958E.description: Describe innovations in theatre technology and presentation techniques from different historical periods

1AA22940DFE601315EEE68A86D17958E.description: Examine how audience behaviors have changed across historical periods and cultures

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Mathematics (PK-8)

BBD87BDAE9474917B3D8206CB07619A2.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

3DF1648A95A745519AD697835A2E414F.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

49B664E2E74A4083A41B6FA23BDC6E17.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

D065B0725AFD4A1BA6C2C079AB257B62.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

B6D58391A50A45B78D1CE309E0E8E4E3.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

B34AE6A2A0784CC9A4095CAFEDD5498C.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events. For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

D173A6EF865C43CF9B50F3DD2689BB5C.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events; compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; and if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

5B758B094A704B4885BDF2DF381E53A5.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability. For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

3902433A6E774DB2B57004B33DECEBCB.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

4A80B6282ECB4088AFBA52664C312087.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

9E28876B72D14389AD86F5D0CAD3D31D.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations. For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

978568FDA7294A0592E27FDD177B7C86.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. For example, mean height of players on the basketball team is. 10 cm greater than mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable

D640BD37275B436E8C04C2E4F7B5E5D9.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

06E8B10DC4574F56A084D24D835B8DB6.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions. For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

21F588DBF4C34116B13FFA0996F9FDB6.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

8462F7713F004E75B7208F285D948AB3.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

8C1A9A95FAF9493D9E971BCEF7E8EBFC.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers; graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem. For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

6EF1E86DAF95454C8B77E1FF10F185F3.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers; solve equations of these forms fluently; compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach. For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

D0409BC9271A419286178CEB6C8F5E26.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

D2A05835F5B74C6DBE8A1AF7C01D86C9.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically; apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies. For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9¾ inches long in the center of a door that is 27½ inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

143E4A6550A747BE9E3AADA5C16B2E37.description: Solve real-life mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

EFF4BAB922074A3985F5077EBC627239.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related. For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

8C4E222C2D714FB38F460777C5D5315C.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

ABDA9A95B302457983E13917E2BA8111.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

713FEB3EA3754D258826EE5B28A5A442.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. (Note: Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.)

0531635941FD4D0A8E0C5DA6590E987D.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; and know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

E76310EAC78C40F6B5E0BB0ECA930EB1.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

63755856A9F641F4A29BBED9F570BF38.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then: -(p/q) = -p/q = p/-q Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

F2F6F180A6E2445481C62C55773D4F56.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

A256F3771AE6425E80C22F71E64EE1C8.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational number.

028C9816D64D4B6B994BC79074C79D69.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

B03ED7B5D47041C0BE83A157EC91A7C4.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

D07CC72FF78547ADB8DF261F41F2B206.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

D11080D32F8B493490DB7ECB7AA7A97D.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.

04BADDCFBBE2470D803385F717CF0330.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, and represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

01D72A7FC4D542D2A3824153D653ACCA.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

BC9C7906B94F457B9A32C608389B5228.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

08652D972ADF4D91A2832BA6EC36EA34.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

80479CB68A46423CB82F19FDAE95617E.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number of n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

C2958416579D493AB585A1BF360679AF.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

4000494411D446EC8A9E4289E8AABDA3.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

2E12B1C450E74AA581260317CEB57020.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

BBC7A9559E684F9CB345710C8CE62638.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like and or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1214 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.

22997FEC57CB4467B0329E85BA923004.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

94FE7924E33F40B89EF10998C97E05E8.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

9533EC2FA37A4876BCE4988DC9101E45.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

B8DBB353C22B44D3B70CCA9BA00B2E37.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

79A178C0AAC749F0B835FC292865C439.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

3988FD85BB0B4136AB9F49D6C56F00C5.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

B63B4A1DC56E43C48ABEEC97C86333DD.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing (drawing?) triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

F5F7E650BB4A42C39C203988906329A4.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

8FA5110209C34B808C567BBD8F2CC1B6.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

98367162AD97474496EB132BEF3EA893.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

6B8E845204D84FF2A6B51F3646DE24C1.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BE0522D0A65A4C09A4D64286EF2F7F8D.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

D45038890FC24A07B4A5B09586B8265B.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

1607C800DFE60131555868A86D17958E.description: Describe ways germs can enter the body.

160735D0DFE60131555668A86D17958E.description: Identify basic ways to prevent the spread of germs.

16066710DFE60131555368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate why it is important to eat at least five servings of fruits and vegetables a day, such as Fruits and Veggies: More Matters.

16061210DFE60131555268A86D17958E.description: Explain the location of the food groups on the My Pyramid.

1605CE50DFE60131555168A86D17958E.description: Recognize the My Pyramid as an outline for healthy eating.

160586C0DFE60131555068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that foods are categorized into groups.

1604E2F0DFE60131554E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how food keeps the body healthy by maintaining strong bones, muscles, and teeth and preventing illness.

16042BD0DFE60131554C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the relationship between food and health.

16036660DFE60131554968A86D17958E.description: Identify the relationship between food and the senses

1602D7E0DFE60131554768A86D17958E.description: Nutrition and Fitness - Students will demonstrate the ability to use nutrition and fitness knowledge, skills, and strategies to promote a healthy lifestyle.

16028910DFE60131554668A86D17958E.description: Model actions to stay safe around strangers.

16022C80DFE60131554568A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to stay safe from strangers.

16017720DFE60131554368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the difference between telling and tattling.

16013000DFE60131554268A86D17958E.description: Define and identify telling and tattling.

1600D9A0DFE60131554168A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of bullying/teasing in the media.

16009550DFE60131554068A86D17958E.description: Discuss examples of bullying including pushing/shoving (physical) and verbal threats.

16000B60DFE60131553E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the characteristics of a bully.

15FF77C0DFE60131553C68A86D17958E.description: Create a list of products in the house that can be harmful.

15FF2A90DFE60131553B68A86D17958E.description: List actions to be safe in the kitchen.

15FEE890DFE60131553A68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to stay safe at home.

15FEA6E0DFE60131553968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate steps for approaching pets or other animals safely.

15FE6460DFE60131553868A86D17958E.description: Show precautions to take around animals.

15FE1EA0DFE60131553768A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to stay safe around animals.

15FD7840DFE60131553568A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to be safe when outdoors.

15FCDEB0DFE60131553368A86D17958E.description: Practice how to respond to an emergency, for example tell an adult and call 911.

15FC8950DFE60131553268A86D17958E.description: Recognize how to respond appropriately to emergency situations.

15FBD830DFE60131553068A86D17958E.description: Safety and Injury Prevention - Students will demonstrate the ability to apply prevention and intervention knowledge, skills, and processes to promote safe living in the home, school, and community.

15FB9760DFE60131552F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how height and weight relate to the growth process.

15FACD90DFE60131552C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize differences in family structure and custom.

15FA8540DFE60131552B68A86D17958E.description: Describe special traits about each member of your family.

15F9E920DFE60131552968A86D17958E.description: Identify what is special about your family.

15F95D90DFE60131552768A86D17958E.description: Family Life and Human Sexuality - Students will demonstrate the ability to use human development knowledge, social skills, and health enhancing strategies to promote positive relationships and health growth and development throughout the life cycle.

15F88380DFE60131552468A86D17958E.description: Identify health issues created by pollution.

15F64570DFE60131551D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how to improve or maintain personal health.

15F5AAE0DFE60131551B68A86D17958E.description: Personal and Consumer Health - Students will demonstrate the ability to use consumer knowledge, skills, and strategies to develop sound personal health practices involving the use of health care products, services, and community resources.

15F56280DFE60131551A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that alcohol is unhealthy and illegal for children.

15F3FE60DFE60131551568A86D17958E.description: Describe the harmful effects of tobacco such as hard to breathe, bad breath, stained teeth, cause disease.

15F37BE0DFE60131551368A86D17958E.description: Identify how tobacco use harms health.

15F111D0DFE60131550B68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe what makes a good choice/decision such as safe, respectful, legal, and parent approval.

15EAE940DFE60131550A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of the word choice/decision.

15EA9B50DFE60131550968A86D17958E.description: Identify how to make a good choice/decision.

15EA1AA0DFE60131550768A86D17958E.description: Identify what makes you happy, upset, calm, and surprised.

15E94980DFE60131550468A86D17958E.description: Examine emotions and responses to various situations.

15E8C670DFE60131550268A86D17958E.description: Define ways to communicate with friends and family, such as eye-contact and tone of voice.

15E7D7A0DFE6013154FF68A86D17958E.description: Mental and Emotional Health - Students will demonstrate the ability to use mental and emotional health knowledge, skills, and strategies to enhance wellness.

1C34E490DFE60131623A68A86D17958E.description:
Identify and describe that ecosystems can be impacted by human activities.
  • Protection of the Chesapeake Bay watershed

1C349D00DFE60131623968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe how environmental change in one part of the world can have consequences for other parts of the world.

1C344F20DFE60131623868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe a range of local issues that have an impact on people in other places.

1C33FA40DFE60131623768A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that human-caused changes have consequences for Maryland's environment as well as for other places and future times.

1C335EB0DFE60131623568A86D17958E.description: Identify possible solutions to problems associated with obtaining, using, and distributing natural resources.

1C7EA990DFE6013162B268A86D17958E.description: Explain how different models can be used to represent the same thing. What kind of a model to use and how complex it should be depend on its purpose.   • Fact and opinion are intermingled
  • Conclusions do not follow logically from the evidence given.
  • Existence of control groups and the relationship to experimental groups is not made obvious.
  • Samples are too small, biased, or not representative

1C79DC20DFE6013162A368A86D17958E.description: Use mathematics to interpret and communicate data.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Mathematics (PK-8)

43E2E9DD61514A58913895A082D09E03.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

A9A6B73DE8F24770A082BF042DEEA8C6.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

357E035620EF43F2951F644F4CBF866B.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

3F15C7EC07AA4985B31FD6C2478CBEE9.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear. For example, the function A= S² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1, 1), (2, 4) and (3, 9), which are not on a straight line.

273E2E0BD82D47D3815FE5D94A42F505.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

4B8FCA664AEB465487E4D8E473157651.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output (function notation is not required in Grade 8).

6D7783264C2C4882B30C573D82BEAD26.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

7C0F33356B7B4A3A8E2A518301C900BB.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

71D4F2FB167743F9B75760EA236373B3.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

D43BDDFE62A54D0E9F3C2A4656937F0C.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

D918038A52FA4338AA2168DDB5A739FB.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

08ECFEC68046470CA707D918FCE8C242.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables. For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

F018C710C794497986A297A15BEF99D0.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection. For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

4A2CBE77DBDD48D48639D507C376896A.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

EAE044D62E774B63937DF1D4E36D0AE4.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations

CADEF472282F4354AFC82917074789C0.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

014C3742C04A4FCF9228BBC2241AD2AC.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (a and b are different numbers).

0D2C4C1B68FE43E68D82EA76159E258A.description: Solve linear equations in one variable

58E8B0351D6240BFBE36A225247E0D77.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

70353A7608E844F296CD7A8FE666B358.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin, and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

B1073AA9FCED4712B1CD6C4D43352872.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

4FC9DF4CD3A843538710856B4F1B6670.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

8FC013B60A6F43A5A6C73738E338A6F5.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

33544BE646DD4732882FA086D8276588.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other. For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

512DF6552AD84631A7B336E9BD946221.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

E6D58F0E4E49471689926F421AF47C60.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 3² × 3<sup>-5</sup> = 3<sup>-3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27

B42EAF1756844110850EA78B77974A56.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

F92250DEE28C4358B948D0D8FD107BEB.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2 , show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

F8ADC4051AFD4F2DB71C942D2DD93B7C.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

521DFFE461324430AA4AAA4400EEBBA8.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

F0CFA8BA0DAE48E09F0A70662BF2FA3B.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

4EE7536D200242518CD8B3F058B1B513.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

6F46F68684654F81833B34A7BFB35A91.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

7C25D7AC6AD047F69E3F5215DD737B41.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

E74361DBC442401FB58ED6A5A6250F47.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

246FDBDF40384910AC85926A50070B6A.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

E6547533384941B7872F7824F7AF2DAC.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

1F6115D9269C412A86EB457B82BF7937.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

EF01D874FD3341B1B246D9F7E9D001A6.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

5648333D877448189C2981E18281D4C6.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.
