17547EC0DFE60131581968A86D17958E.description: List reasons why people get pregnant such as by accident, not using contraception, to keep a partner, to have a child to love, not being abstinent

175439E0DFE60131581868A86D17958E.description: Assess the impact of unplanned pregnancy on the teen, the child and the family.

1753F4F0DFE60131581768A86D17958E.description: Determine the impact of teen pregnancy.

17524DD0DFE60131581268A86D17958E.description: Explain the gestation process of fetal development and maternal changes.

1751A940DFE60131581068A86D17958E.description: Examine reasons why people have sexual intercourse, such as desire to have someone to love, alcohol/drug influence, partner pressure, media influence, curiosity, and to gain social status.

17515AE0DFE60131580F68A86D17958E.description: Develop ways to maintain abstinence in a relationship. c. Model skills to resist peer pressure to have sexual intercourse.

17510B30DFE60131580E68A86D17958E.description: Validate the reasons why abstinence from sexual activity is a healthy, safe, and responsible decision for adolescents.

1750B6B0DFE60131580D68A86D17958E.description: Investigate factors that influence an individual's decision concerning sexual behavior.

17500140DFE60131580B68A86D17958E.description: Prioritize and demonstrate the components of a healthy relationship in a variety of situations.

174FAE00DFE60131580A68A86D17958E.description: Justify the components of a healthy relationship, including respect for self and others, effective communication, honesty, support, empathy, and ability to resolve conflicts in rational, peaceful way

174F6250DFE60131580968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the components of a healthy relationship.

174ED940DFE60131580768A86D17958E.description: Explain the stages of the menstrual cycle and its connection to a woman's overall health.

174E48F0DFE60131580568A86D17958E.description: Describe the process of the menstrual cycle.

174D8DC0DFE60131580368A86D17958E.description: Investigate factors that influence stereotyping and generalizations about gender.

174D3A40DFE60131580268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how family members influence the development of adolescents

174C92A0DFE60131580068A86D17958E.description: Family Life and Human Sexuality - Students will demonstrate the ability to use human development knowledge, social skills, and health enhancing strategies to promote positive relationships and health growth and development throughout the life cycle.

174C3E20DFE6013157FF68A86D17958E.description: Describe society's responsibility for maintaining and improving the quality and availability of health care from health clinics, physicians, Medicaid/Medicare, governmental agencies, and community based organizations

174BF5F0DFE6013157FE68A86D17958E.description: Access and evaluate health information, products, and services in order to become health literate consumers.

174B6350DFE6013157FC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how health behaviors and use of health services are influenced by diversity, such as family traditions, social/cultural customs, religious beliefs, geographic locations (access to services), and economic status.

174B12A0DFE6013157FB68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the negative consequences of behaviors, including tattoos, body piercings, and sharing health products.

174AA890DFE6013157FA68A86D17958E.description: Access and evaluate health enhancing behaviors and reduce health risks to live safer, healthier lives.

1749D5B0DFE6013157F868A86D17958E.description: Personal and Consumer Health - Students will demonstrate the ability to use consumer knowledge, skills, and strategies to develop sound personal health practices involving the use of health care products, services, and community resources.

17498760DFE6013157F768A86D17958E.description: Assess the consequences of steroid abuse.

17492F00DFE6013157F668A86D17958E.description: Discriminate between medical use and the abuse of steroids.

1748B890DFE6013157F568A86D17958E.description: Identify types and uses of steroids.

174858E0DFE6013157F468A86D17958E.description: Determine appropriate and inappropriate use of steroids and the consequences of each.

1747C3F0DFE6013157F268A86D17958E.description: Describe the consequences of use and abuse of psychoactive drugs.

174780E0DFE6013157F168A86D17958E.description: Examine the use and abuse of psychoactive drugs.

17473BD0DFE6013157F068A86D17958E.description: Compare different classifications of drugs, including hallucinogens, stimulants, depressants, and narcotics.

1746EF60DFE6013157EF68A86D17958E.description: Classify a variety of psychoactive drugs and identify the consequences of their use and abuse.

174650A0DFE6013157ED68A86D17958E.description: Investigate specific laws governing alcohol, including Blood Alcohol Level/Blood Alcohol Content (BAL/BAC), moving vehicles (DUI), cultural (religious and home), and purchasing (fake ID, underage, other buyers).

17460960DFE6013157EC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the legal ramifications of alcohol use and abuse in a variety of situations.

1745C5E0DFE6013157EB68A86D17958E.description: Investigate support services and community resources for assistance and treatment, including Alcoholics Anonymous (AA), Al-Anon, and Alateen.

174581F0DFE6013157EA68A86D17958E.description: Explore diseases caused by alcohol abuse such as cirrhosis and Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS).

17453B80DFE6013157E968A86D17958E.description: Describe how addiction impacts family and society.

1744E560DFE6013157E868A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of addiction on individuals and society and identify resources for rehabilitation.

1743F6A0DFE6013157E568A86D17958E.description: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Other Drugs - Students will demonstrate the ability to use drug knowledge, decision making skills, and health enhancing strategies to address, the use, non-use, and abuse of medications, alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.

174347E0DFE6013157E368A86D17958E.description: Identify resources that address depression and suicide.

1742F150DFE6013157E268A86D17958E.description: Identify warning signs of depression, suicide and/or other destructive behaviors.

1741D730DFE6013157DF68A86D17958E.description: Construct a plan to achieve a personal wellness goal.

17418BE0DFE6013157DE68A86D17958E.description: Develop a goal to adopt, maintain or improve a personal wellness habit.

17413870DFE6013157DD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate strategies, skills and resources that are used to achieve personal goals.

1740F090DFE6013157DC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how changing information, abilities, priorities, and responsibilities influence personal goals.

1740A9C0DFE6013157DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the importance of setting goals.

174061F0DFE6013157DA68A86D17958E.description: Implement a strategy and evaluate progress toward achieving personal goals.

173FCC40DFE6013157D868A86D17958E.description: Devise a plan that addresses personal strengths, needs, and health risks.

173F8280DFE6013157D768A86D17958E.description: Compose a personal health goal and measure progress towards its achievement.

173F30E0DFE6013157D668A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of assuming responsibilities of personal health behavior.

173EDAB0DFE6013157D568A86D17958E.description: Apply the components of personal well-being to develop lifelong wellness skills and strategies.

173DDB60DFE6013157D268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate effective communication in everyday situations.

173D9A50DFE6013157D168A86D17958E.description: Utilize/model strategies to overcome barriers when communicating information, ideas, emotions, and opinions.

173D1140DFE6013157CF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and apply effective communication skills.

173C3850DFE6013157CD68A86D17958E.description: Mental and Emotional Health - Students will demonstrate the ability to use mental and emotional health knowledge, skills, and strategies to enhance wellness.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Mathematics (PK-8)

2294ADAC1379454DA05C5CC38E371A10.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

B35ED448BC644075985DFD553CD83ACC.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients. For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.

61B0A93699754C8D8D9DC5D34BF7B87A.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients. For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4 and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.

F74CCAD5F8554B9CB3EB33ABB1532980.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions. (Students able to multiply fractions in general can develop strategies to divide fractions in general, by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division. But division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade.)

F7F79BA8E61547D68AFB7812883E2D5A.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem

CB5E98950A5147CC806A860E2C40EC6C.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than one results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n × a)/(n × b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

36380D01E1E84DB28CC51C7E26867D40.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

0B9EE9EB2DC546F9A4770FDA43507421.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

7E25F813176241FB815A60E93B6BAC6C.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.)

3FA0697004A44F5AA8458437C5B148D7.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

E342C6613A3747A6AA18D8B2EAC41CA6.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. For example, interpret 3/4 as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that 3/4 multiplied by 4 equals 3 and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

220BF46BD08D4D2E94EBD027DFC9E20D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

8CD9DF922F6F43418CDE91D149E8E13A.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers. For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7 by observing that 3/7 < 1/2.

FD652E179A3E443DB87C82A5B50DD1CE.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators. For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12+ 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd)

F8FFCD0B80DF48F096B19374929E21F7.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

779E502D105A4079932C0385BED761ED.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

C71AA26F96594125BEB36829D9D20432.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category. For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

191ED049AC1F4AD0AE58A1C1E9237780.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

DDA7A71C9BC547E0B9D2683C9966CF95.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

4F34D9448C2543BD9983C1CDA78D1171.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

0E1D6270152546B58CE317B0D6D9D6B8.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

C54D8E42014B4D80B0D87BCF07B67846.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

41A0C4D40F894134BE068330BAD7C93D.description: Apply the formulas V =(l)(w)(h) and V = (b)(h) for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of .solving real world and mathematical problems.

1A5F25F2AE1D469D9C7F13ED6F019501.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent three-fold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

4B54712E625F4761B679DB715A2DB329.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

6CBDD7519AD34AC9B8275B52DA448A41.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

31CFEE7F87A8409BB4544D06F7DD6996.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

DA418475B2F946E98FEE2FAD44EEF277.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

2A0F7D335FBC4FD0AA60EE32E6DE8DEB.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

29BB696CBD7B4A5E905692FC8F5BF738.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

88D9DD397A8747C4A2DAC31BE462F230.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots. For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.

CF3A07CE6D6648FFAAC440828071EF0E.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step real world problems.

3447E7E754C44C838F2F1B5C627B960C.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

10AAD9A1769D467A998BE3E1D43D34F8.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

80DA3D6C0FD141C993AF0B538B00E4B6.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

BB3DF76976EA4803B704665D06EEB3EF.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

AD05C908D1614081B5723597B781D11D.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place

5CF74BCCA71E455EAF76B6D9EA81C69F.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

047CA621AE28455A836782BF86D803C0.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

8AD64571B37340D6BAF9CA9561DEF55A.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

561D7777CFD047848157F92C3AAC687C.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

CD68BA515F8845C29FA1D043E470857C.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

40C697559F3F43CC99601E02F396A5E6.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole number exponents to denote powers of 10.

875C24EAEDDA41A4B56F65396CFC005C.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 110 of what it represents in the place to its left.

512A24D7709A4F919733186815D83F29.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

D7EEA12DD88344A5BE02B9FE10E05FF3.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

3DD85355114B41E2BD69E0C8DBCA5C0E.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

C5C9E22DFA0343FB9F1C5D8FAA6B1746.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

2EAEDB2B86D7453983A6E50F068A9DF4.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

D349094E52764CCCA205A26B6FA3A772.description: Look for and make use of structure.

B3457BF3030840DB8A50CA201B60D535.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

7FA0CAEC711E40128422535736382DB5.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - Geometry

E981C5276FDF4F72B87D4E2BC51E515D.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects. (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

9FC3A7C0FA9C4C939CFC8CCED9834AC9.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

1F5F36AC07FA4741844FE2E33CDEF565.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.; for example prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

D728CE13A54F454595A989CB7D486DE7.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

39B0E6C35E654A64B8C0B1D062104DF7.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

92C2A70B40534808AAE7C5D300AE6872.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

31829179152747A0B16B33A4F44CA2BD.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

46FF8D2ABB354C71A30724BBC571F1D9.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

F46240D52E8049DB983F96E4ABCB96E6.description: (+) Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

D66378148C0F498EBE929FC1AFEFEA9B.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

9B5C62BAF5AC44DD89808AFC54171E26.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

706FBF68F3E449B6B5F5D977C53B5DAD.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

1C97684C75DA4F2ABE9D134B61793B3A.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

60881BD2617E4EDFA9213002149054AD.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

C6C8CDF9C21145E6809E17E098036AB5.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

B1FE273600364801AA1CCDA80AFB118F.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

E89503A828184AEA987F5042D7C32A29.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle.

6027EC2EB0E645198838DD712FC66D88.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

A28D92FB56904DA3BBFFE4862FDD7D23.description: Connecting Algebra and Geometry Through Coordinates

728581E7E028485EB6829A142D7B10B3.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

9767A3A52B994247A8E1D1049EAAEC77.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

1146916E60DA4C81A2F3DE0C0D63DE23.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

89CA3854734944D3AE82BFD47F6CABD2.description: Visualize the relation between two dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

3843BF819BAD49DC9CD0DCF167576A8D.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

D84DA836086543C38982E9B952576DAE.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

33448CCDD5B24483970ADF0FB3A545BB.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

11179ED9013540D4AB575FC0B282C3D6.description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

EB3F492E1276462FBA24441A6BA95FD4.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

7D7A36801A0B4DCA881E0127F041404A.description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

282D080020E14B238C2F53B661524DB7.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

E4D371D4DFB7401EA5E7628010401EEA.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

BECA48BB1F0648E59E1DA88A2D8B658D.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects. (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

F3A7F24348284FB595C80A5F1AAA4E1A.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

F70D9503E78F4CBFBCE64F314DD94CB2.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

B8CD1CB2ACCE4F91A89B476F95EA9EF5.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

AB4637FADC444612BE190CA5993C75C9.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

FC686E8CAB5A4D68BD210421075468A6.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

DAB5C6CEB3614C61B56B49601E63A347.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

C3B021C43CA44591B1706FC18918B77F.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

21B087A438384FA6941A38E44E84AF33.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

FB78F657213E4EF7A106C8EB898EA12E.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

FB8A9CC8362549C9B9B6FB72544D5083.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

DB102013C9B94A7E84F6F3A38E306191.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

B86F7DE506A140AE854A3CDB8D0A8FA8.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

42DA56CE41204F21A1C859A53F672546.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

B1FD67D4B65C422FA327FB856AF69D2F.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

515F6479210E4CF19302C3CD6A20586A.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

38514EF9C440494895F3E12CA985A19E.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

F3715A68CD9645DE8B8D55CB18C113F0.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

9247799BEF4046FA9B15A3EF5D6B2737.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

E11BF4955EC74796A3D389A97B9B66CA.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

4E961A76945447F98439E202108A2EBC.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

41514603C063467AAE0E0590A40D9EA7.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

FCCA431D356F4E49AA417DA260567C16.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

B81A2DA9F4384C89B397669B8D7E0197.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

B27AD301D649400898D51872B82099A0.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

6ABA9CEBF0E6452C8BA036D29B446DEB.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

A591F7D24AD543729D72AB7D339EA51F.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch)

27F4EFBFBA5C4210B023CCD3CCE828B7.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

A2BAD5CD62AA43538BAE3F8EC7E3C56B.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

E57E68E5C5F844CAAA00AC26D3C11B8B.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

9E45DB2766E64F2AA716B9D418900997.description: Look for and make use of structure.

2D5F9087C5AE45A98DB0AEF8AA421B36.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

7073B553F9FA48209F5B41DBA9A963A7.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

18E6E6E0DFE601315B2A68A86D17958E.description: Identify conventions of audience etiquette and how they relate to dance performances

18E69CE0DFE601315B2968A86D17958E.description: Recognize selected characteristics of the elements of dance, such as body parts and positions, shapes and levels, tempo, directions, general and personal space, and percussive and sustained energy, in performances

18E64B40DFE601315B2868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe selected aesthetic principles, such as repetition, unity, variety, and sequence, in dance performances

18E5FF60DFE601315B2768A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply criteria to evaluate choreography and performance

18E5C0E0DFE601315B2668A86D17958E.description: Aesthetics and Criticism: Students will demonstrate the ability to make aesthetic judgments in dance.

18E58170DFE601315B2568A86D17958E.description: Complete simple dances from beginning to end incorporating an awareness of space in relationship to other dancers and the performance area

18E541E0DFE601315B2468A86D17958E.description: Describe how awareness of space affects dance presentation

18E50170DFE601315B2368A86D17958E.description: Develop knowledge and execution of performance competencies in dance

18E4B370DFE601315B2268A86D17958E.description: Use choreographic forms, such as narrative and theme and variation, to communicate ideas through dance movement

18E429D0DFE601315B2068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate movement effects using repetition and sequence

18E469C0DFE601315B2168A86D17958E.description: Communicate movement ideas using combinations of the elements of dance

18E3E5D0DFE601315B1F68A86D17958E.description: Communicate movement ideas using combinations of the elements of dance

18E39950DFE601315B1E68A86D17958E.description: Develop the ability to combine the elements, aesthetic principles, and choreographic forms of dance to communicate meaning

18E351E0DFE601315B1D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret ideas from stories, poems, or songs, using improvisation

18E2EC30DFE601315B1C68A86D17958E.description: Improvise variations on given movement patterns through manipulation of body and space

18E2A320DFE601315B1B68A86D17958E.description: Improvise movements in response to teacher and self-initiated stimuli

18E26140DFE601315B1A68A86D17958E.description: Develop the ability to improvise dance

18E221B0DFE601315B1968A86D17958E.description: Creative Expression and Production: Students will demonstrate the ability to create and perform dance.

18E1E090DFE601315B1868A86D17958E.description: Explore ways line, shape, time, and movement are used in dance and other content areas

18E19B70DFE601315B1768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the relationships between and among dance and other content areas

18E13CE0DFE601315B1668A86D17958E.description: Create movements that express contrasting moods

18E0DEE0DFE601315B1568A86D17958E.description: View and discuss selected contemporary and historical dance styles from other times and places, label them as old or new, and tell why

18E0A2B0DFE601315B1468A86D17958E.description: Relate dance to history, society, and personal experience

18E06660DFE601315B1368A86D17958E.description: Perform selected traditional dances from various cultures using a variety of formations and partnering

18E02A10DFE601315B1268A86D17958E.description: View selected dances from a variety of cultures and identify their purposes

18DFEDA0DFE601315B1168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of dances from a variety of cultures

18DFADE0DFE601315B1068A86D17958E.description: Historical, Cultural, and Social Context: Students will demonstrate an understanding of dance as an essential aspect of history and human experience.

18DF6520DFE601315B0F68A86D17958E.description: Select specific movements and describe their purposes

18DF2400DFE601315B0E68A86D17958E.description: Apply the language of danceto observed movement from different genres

18DEDF80DFE601315B0D68A86D17958E.description: Respond to dance through observation, experience, and analysis

18DD7DA0DFE601315B0868A86D17958E.description: Associate selected dance movements with specific dance genres

18DD3D90DFE601315B0768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate kinesthetic awareness and technical proficiency in dance performance

18DE9550DFE601315B0C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate balance and timing in directed movement experiences

18DE51E0DFE601315B0B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate locomotor and non-locomotor movements using kinesthetic awareness

18DE1160DFE601315B0A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate kinesthetic awareness and technical proficiency in dance movement

18DCFAA0DFE601315B0668A86D17958E.description: Combine selected characteristics of the elements of dance, such as body parts and positions, shapes, levels, directions, general and personal space, energy, and tempo, and use sensory stimuli to create movement

18DCB7C0DFE601315B0568A86D17958E.description: Identify and demonstrate basic locomotor and non-locomotor movements that communicate ideas, thoughts, and feelings

18DC73C0DFE601315B0468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how elements of dance are used to communicate meaning

18DC1A90DFE601315B0368A86D17958E.description: Perceiving, Performing, and Responding: Aesthetic Education - Students will demonstrate the ability to perceive, perform, and respond to dance.

document.title: Maryland College and Career-Ready Standards - English Language Arts

E22C217AEB4F47A58E031F4A060F1158.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

F0ACAD15AFA04B5F82CD7A001BB922D0.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

EBC7825E05FE4E83B1AF45BC5C7BB335.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1B67421E16AF4D6DA09D9BBE99CBA22A.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grade 4 on pages 28 and 29.)

C95BDFC3B90345B3BB88E42D8B77E3C1.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

013E4808003A41799C9EDB5C25284559.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to the task, purpose and audience.

86E3EC61EF6D4EF0AC443D84C7AC209E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

C80BEAD7EBD94DCBA88433B92CB9C1A4.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

BFF9B20EF8244B34A9BA9FC3CCC74E9E.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

1FC9ABC5388A4EEBBDEC25C585175122.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

82868C24DCF340A4979097EFB21BD086.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

6CE938A0D9804DD48D10B244BD1B6154.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

7597D310B48548BD8DDECBCBBC3963E5.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

3A959CCEC9BC479D8286AC6E93D4A88B.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

00AEA97A98124B7688315999FCEC6063.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

258394E883E7419FA110E98315D9CFD3.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

9A8E4866560441DEA40EFF24017F4513.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

1374D99657744CD6B87BAEC2B67ABA6D.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

B92E106D76364B16A9DE7A1576C966E2.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

92888918B6CA4059ABFDA079B359301E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

E55CC56007904BB481618DE452126A44.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

02B2504457614B01BE5793E9F25635C3.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

D9607310BBFE48B2A44B9F851B5298CC.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

934537E4B5BB445BB9C85D2F85CE54FC.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

B084A76A610B413F8DE4415CA1B8A683.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

82517EEA7DE14F28B824C648E08E61DF.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

22074C5825F64CEEA0FCE8C598C3915D.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

2F150060106D4FDA9492F1C2BA175C01.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

F4385F3DACBA4CAB877916816CD28ADA.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

E0CE725491E8401F89837918EB8A65C9.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

F90942F00DE148A09C866128D891224B.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

29C25AEBEE2C4DC8A8589E6A1E39F2DC.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A2DB00E97AF64CB88925ECCD2A17AB09.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

55DB892B640745F488110F053AA4CD64.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

E68CDD250B7443BDA6BA6312EBF85521.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

5EC7980AC4D8478FBB530C3EFFF01FEE.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

136B30968ADD4FA18F40F220E0706BE9.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

ABEFA8E9AF7848E5B90CBDE6DDA43361.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

BCCB875191C541379F03A4975F942478.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

ED73A31D7BA24F8F8C6A9E0BF6851191.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

AAA34A40251246BA82214131BB5E3268.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F2AC2A79305D493FAC3396F00931E4E9.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

AEB9BE33E3844B05B815D3C5E6755CE5.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

21AF40F01EBD495BB0B565968B553E6D.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

36E158DB58D7464FBF4EF521AC8B468B.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

6FAE7C52A2EA44768661E27EF08567D5.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

374ACAB273C744BA967E1D9FA23391FA.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

1898CBFA205E4645AEE9B363DA46AF98.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

F977B1187EE242C38995030B323B8E4F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

EBA5CB0AB96344AF9BD091FEA248A78A.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

F2EC64C2E44B43ECAD086CBC15AD5492.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

4B8B6FD8711D4F2FA9D089FE30B558FD.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

FB1430D654724606AD095D837D65D2CA.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

C8BAA0C154FA4DC98F70B3F180B2233F.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

C36708FAE07A4B7B9A572DCEA38F1816.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

01F515DE21E847DDA94DA0465391B725.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

B9100FD11E08412EAC5479C552F4A31D.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

2515EC016D754F28B9C64561F73BD116.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

93914F9C76224DEEAF2D8D780359FAE0.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

E258E85739614714A82A6B86B4C13F5E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

816573492490419192D3E58B8D6078AE.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data was gathered.

703798B832884FD188F3AA1642AE98ED.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number

6A1AEB4B93C34218819CC5101A7A7BB6.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

3C8BCE14A4ED457D8ADEC7E264C72390.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers. For example, "How old am I?" is not a statistical question, but "How old are the students in my school?" is a statistical question because one anticipates variability in students' ages.

6141D2510ACA402EBD11CFA76D172E5F.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation. For example, in a problem involving motion at constant speed, list and graph ordered pairs of distances and times, and write the equation d = 65t to represent the relationship between distance and time.

421F234557264386BA9FCB17DB5A78BF.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

C763750D45844ADF895FF8088FCFA01E.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. 84ADA9D0813E4E2AB462C2534D6E2621.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers.

3532621C3D7F495ABDC365CC8192FF43.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

60E8003AE60047AC82BC594DDCDEF65D.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? 6226A2B9F2AE45E3A8EC69C93387A02D.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

For example, the expressions y + y + y and 3y are equivalent because they name the same number regardless of which number y stands for.

8AA67E6F3B314D83A4DD4167B74BE351.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions. For example, apply the distributive property to the expression 3(2 + x) to produce the equivalent expression 6 + 3x; apply the distributive property to the expression 24x + 18y to produce the equivalent expression 6 (4x + 3y); apply properties of operations to y + y + y to produce the equivalent expression 3y.

E21E797BA80146FABC92D815EC3AF64B.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values for their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas in real-world problems.
