3217199AEABD45E494AA4E093EDF5ACF.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole- number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent three-fold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

DECE6F6F99004FE1BDBA02A04161D5FC.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition, and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

F5ADBED73E5548C9A13F07E2E8E41029.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

A5F3D3BE22ED447CA2A746B93BEA1B0D.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

2898E913FF2F44D5A9E05D6E7469DD81.description: A cube with side lengths 1 unit, called a "unit cube", is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

60E0CCB93E3C476089C816DFC261D819.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

50FFCE5895B24E69BCE26571BA0F32A1.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

A3582BBFECDF4B12908092C07EB70F94.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8), Use operations for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

C7B16B2F8BD54753BFF6A96373EEC632.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m).

C5FF6F6BFEE74111834E3B30BEE0609C.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

8FBFCED7348B4016A60565D8954B319E.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

29285EC9FD9249ECB52FA6AE9A265817.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.

EC4FB154612F4BE086E4678459D166D3.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

D72AD995AAFD412099F8BA631045C5FE.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions. Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

AC9DE91A5D224CF0923405D806677B0A.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

2DDF3E2522544241B0418B3784785809.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than one results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n × a)/ (n × b) to the effect of multiplying (a/b) by 1.

BDEBAC8A876C4462823156A80B406203.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

3EC7E76BF97749599DA431777205237E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

E3F5EB435E9641BFB050CCF52788E02F.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a part of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.

5A9143521A2D4119BCB4213F417CAA0B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

D3F9B4C431E6475281375C17B5E25291.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

55698BDD0A3D4CDC95A23E4B1904A9F5.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

55FDA695E00C4E16B72D4870C06BA0D1.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

DF8078FBEBF1493EA82F9EFE38169DC6.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

15C850F214ED45AE8F2B69909162FB97.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

0BB16D9BC72F4CCAA7F555ED4A7AF98E.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

B5E6A2D293AD4584B21CBCACE18F1956.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D322A76DAB5F4CF0B98C6A67874459E8.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

5BF4D623633942668C4D774F6864BE4B.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

B2B9159C59AF40ACB10E83D21AB6DDF9.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

670B2F5175E34EE29FAB665F7B6AD0F3.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

7262CC76033B48CD8442CC08C1214C4F.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g. 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000)

FAFFFCC6AD2C4A089CCFA68F9A8A8252.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

E407568D0CBF4638A2C417CA6A9E0481.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole number exponents to denote powers of 10.

BAED5A37531447F7BE65931894ED4209.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

3CD5573C214345C3BD889F8EBE47F20A.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

C55115F318184A118FE8380436EF2C01.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

5D9C4671CDD34CCE8A721C00DC83C1C8.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Algebra I

16213E2A77074763AC6D8E82268EDC03.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

68C764E2C7174ABBA48417C7C778D7DF.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

6B7E09E3C8B24FFF802AA3F0810ECCD0.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

19D41B0F3AD14D05BB10CEE7A0E31427.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

2CEC9E5C863448A9AEC7DA2B5183C558.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

EAB9B559EA3840B790845469184A3BA4.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

BFE92C3F2C964381A3D00A3748C462F3.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

828E8217046147A8969496B2CAF313A3.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

D07C8CF98C54412880258AC4F0BCA5FA.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

12B3E52F43AF4315BF7865B2A10164A6.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

C587D88E82164BC3955D719A419DA194.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

ABB97302472F4AE39A2CA6102AAE4447.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

76B99AE3A13F4AB1B74BB360099A8C2A.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

3E920852B89B441B8FFD9DF446F57DCF.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

C4C0685F23834771B501036F1F30FF55.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

18C012C9B8364C0F9C8C5DA934E77B89.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

FC80CB61BAE741988D1AD0B11C77A469.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

618F4F5BEEDC4CE39709065F4F527B64.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

BCC4A60B30ED47A9ABB6F9416C312540.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

43B91B9E070D4F468608719A3C6E66A8.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

650DFDEAEE884644A96E88D70A05C5AC.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

53F1BF0BFFB741BEB69AB5B7528D7975.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

310B9EB51C0142D59DCA8D7BCBF76B5E.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

9C117FB801264D36ADF72B0C4A556169.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

73DDDDE399824F6BB7B5788063BCA94B.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

A536EFD7710A4EF5A14CD40DC0811EA5.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

20A8601723AF46FEB8FD618396B33CBA.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

9A165DE1F8074E12B2564E0E74CAC4E6.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

3FE3399026A940E0962EABADA0A5F6EC.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

D96682AC7BAF4BA3AD8148BFE15C44F6.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

33856C6009C24E859F3BB209FE9D9494.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

F66CAE3AD6C34C28879B563C5DF888BE.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

B9598F8F33C2440AB0D54FEDBBFD496C.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

618947E17D734E16A8545DE789251DCA.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

A294D1A5D5DE49E999B8CBFF1A1489B4.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

A6D919EBDBB943BD878748DA56CCFB3C.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

0753A9F76A874F968C62297CF28B897E.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n + 1) = f(n) + f(n - 1) for n ≥ 1.

3B9110E9B373409C8E8D83C7342DA966.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

CB7EC314331844FA82C3140EDCE04938.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

04A806FE63B0408DB87FE65B47BCB41F.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

627C8ED13F234D21A9C4814662420997.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

562580334ACF413F811996AEC515AD1E.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

34887FB02C6C45ED8346FA7CC1F2FBA1.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

3D9D7BD54B8942BE9E6CE4640988A566.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

ACE059BD5D3B4C9D9151117E52DCBA99.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

96B268BA58FE454A903DA9CAE47A4656.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

58A78DDF1BB74D51882E4C6AC69FC9D5.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

EE126BF45C024939BAE64B7362A4484D.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

A235CFDE804342379A42178FD8D7A654.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

EAD3CD7A20EB4DD59F2942FF1F8F59E3.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

FF47D59EF8A94650B93E4AD271C47F95.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

142276CB6EAA45918D9DDF1037712DDD.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

527A01E9D03546A7A69B88F16A133F72.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

64F5873807164EE6A6A6F9AD9C8EBDFC.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

7A5620625B2C4AE988F76B3C108386BA.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

FA6F3583023E432B87F47BFFE918FCA4.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

C907FA26C5604062B9442900CE9E0E30.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

169F9FEAE47A466E90A6811B3B44F99D.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

D2C2C1AEA0FB4E97AC213AAFC947FB97.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

81E3F5CB593A47DEBA482220E2531C78.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

7A2DC916C1FD42C7A890F80823D69366.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

8430A6F3EAE0424C8D5778EE3C63B092.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

69F8A53B702A4C028A2D26ED0A76294B.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

6B25B30547FB4D3EAEBFA98461B33913.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

00450CD0195D4DDF988E37679FCD09D8.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

8AB14CC8D00046A3BD35BE8AD1F630EA.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

3A0BC31756E441809F3377EAE252E991.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

7DEED5DFC5984B4E8CBAE25D395432F6.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

F44C5B5306C24B6180DF9428E737CE9E.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

FD0ED79CA95A4610BD9D42D2373F84F5.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

8880F334A9A540E0BD84314CC9C0CA2B.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

3CC251AAC22444E5950B12B709C04308.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

7A3F52B8D4A94376BF6824091C7489B8.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling. Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

F4DC1DEF66A54BC4B1C1D3D353356FEB.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

DD0EB20EC16B488781BD44C06177942F.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

DA4059C0425B49A98B03153504ADF4E8.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

E30DC66AA9444869ABB93EDC8478ECF4.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Algebra II

619E86B84CCC435DAA9CF4138474A15E.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

FBEC827CCEFC4EBB8D47AF0E52F89531.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

693AC59EDE8749ECBBFD951A47320216.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

584A3DBC5FCB44D7B12A3D304BDC1646.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

260EF2A26638418CBFDC2A77715B1020.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

6D82CCE2C40A4868874A4854FB9BFE85.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

27A1D5406F4D4B6EBC2675B3EF25A8D8.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

D3EA5D29FA1A474F87F5057414BCC33B.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

E0BA9267586C448EB181F3767F093D70.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data

9BF490131D0C499D9268827885E6E792.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

E9D821498E15460DB472B27EB3E37CCD.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

F937D184B08541499686C8745A62B417.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

65434A195AA54626947A7D0F6EE42788.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

CFB85A9D23054A0BA93F23AA41D9B625.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments and observational studies.

20448DE57CED4810800718ABAE486311.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.

F9CD3D57C0B648A0AEEF3BF73E5D436D.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

AEEB670459864EEBA0CBDFDB9D7B0600.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

FD973A72E7E840B3B61F2B3462980034.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

70CBAC6CB02C4AD5A0D980156E858F2B.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

072CD8C1CA9C40EAAFE237B1754A40A1.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

FFB60138ED8C404D8934A1A723D3E600.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

360F0EA937664D27B75529CA68B0C3D8.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

74FDDE5279AB43B0977C7A76191E5E5D.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

4D7401BD135944ED89E426AB5C6FDFA2.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

125E16C16B41493AB9DB63945CAAE2ED.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

132FD1389BD7468FA26BD49969DBBE08.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

B819A59D7CD74C9188AD28C9EB1D44FC.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

A77F51943A5D4D0D8B67B32129241054.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

F275F641E62340B3AB9C034FE534570C.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

7AF78BB3FE054C1581077909E6EA13A0.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

9E6AE19546D74030AFCEAD940A75F53A.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

D290A62BCF0249EDA7677F2369C1E85E.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

BB07B448AE144C12AC22D401D3C19CDE.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abct = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

D3AA6558517B40D3A363D23BC2A8E24D.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

A9670BD5462E47569912FA9DC99A2075.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

6C6EC27AAE58484BBF492CC38E33EE19.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse.

C3CAAF2FCAC74B9BBB24518CDD7053A4.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

4AF79FB531BD4FEF894BDAB31EE83ED0.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

586ECE551F3E42CFB4DBADFCEE6F96CF.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

7CA7511F7F434553B714C715D9BF704A.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

DB7425A60D7F452F8A413AD944B25608.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

A3D3A9CC28494DEEBDCB757814817CF2.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

0D2C62E284B141438B0F601B678AB560.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

389D9A5861D34832B55DF652910C53F0.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

179094D2699B445D9739819A8FC296AB.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

1AE3BF856DF144C4B3BF7A0B70A1128A.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

5DFED7D7512447869670D5DB3001F137.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

8B06D02816234929938EBF7CA4AB7BC1.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

6D0813C3F7B34CF6867111FBBAAD89CD.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

19E0A783BF00409293A296EBF0177EE9.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

AF88E5D0E22349A2958E42CA9573CBA6.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

AF7914CEF07F4964BA366B4B63C498E3.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

AFE2C866F1694C9EBD0AC05D1DE7586F.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

420DEB653A79471A88DE7A1462588F86.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

09AD1E651E254BE8905E6EFAD7EA06DE.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

FDF7A52617874BDA82A7AF530A60FC3F.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

F51D790FBC3D440A898E623F320675FF.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

AAA248DDD1354EC78188D3ADFC8318AB.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

C77CC99A2AFF490AB3F7F3F57519A65D.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

A0B30C9FA9D4434EAFD111F370CB75BA.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

6228E52BBF2E4526A35645FBBA984A58.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

037D6096CA1F4EF5890F421CFCD85BDA.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49, taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

1D5A1971A2A740AC99FD690F6846EDF5.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

F3F89A521FA94517B3F6ACB167C11193.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

A366C5D683B04B87A5AEA209904C0650.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

5E3082DD82F142DE998FA0CFA88A5365.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

5FFDD5B1235F4597B8D96FA401E56063.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

7BBB617BF04C433A826FF8E778A24A63.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

29B7834BDAF5457681F4BB6F67C2AE91.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

B596A71CF5E2411FB91B12B7F163403B.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

443D5C55CB244D14ADFA39962F4CA892.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

79DF6776BCFF4EFBA82A12327A7431D7.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

37BDFE50E87D4E3290471F97CD835C57.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

AC1746BA68BE40618C5792D0C54D2CCA.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

059075075D164567B91182F6C9C5B835.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

0955724C3098456BB417D31D9BDBD0F3.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

8E875B6FE02943539049BDB02B567202.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

0F2FCA3539DF4BD1B876CB27A4F4F63E.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

304B66002E704666ADAD4A35A6EBF97F.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

B44EB2FF49AC41CDA5B28D5C8936734D.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

51C0B27884F847248A4EB78D1E12AAEC.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

2DD551FB4D3F45869A0DBB92A22406B7.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

D1E95092FB4A42608077E2C5FCF49099.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

BFEF2714A314446BB3D5FC8746E2C536.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

308AA914685C4A73A6B9E5F019633BE6.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

9CB6B6C4183448CB84B7F1581110F3CF.description: Use the relation i² = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

0A19B27E19214D559CD4613D4E9AA25E.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² =-1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

AD689D1AFE93453D811464D4358B7864.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

36472DB4D0F449788B3C3173D4C96E34.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

B46645D22F80415EB5D4DA90207F3C78.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

91A37E46023B497AAD9BB1D3F5B93B43.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

FAE3374F3BDE4E959AD2F290EA237C0A.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

46660B63410C43F5847B0360DB0D0244.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 3

4488150A1E6E42278287FEFE0C8C0896.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

74571B961D5640F9B4ABE9B360BBB16F.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

310813E66EDD4B25AA6E1AC24BC3B22C.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

51B6E481EEF04D409EB68EA08B1A498A.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

CDD2A094B5414008BC1D6C11A2097F85.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

B30B23C2983648B4A29274D091372338.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

BF0E8469DDB242198D1A0F620D681678.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a x b and a x c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

D76C81FE56404910B4E734E99497A421.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

5A7AA80FEDA54DFEB491930B1C63CD65.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

AE42C6230CDA4C979269D6DD77DCEE93.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

99BD8E2E90B740DEA9BB70A35EA1CF45.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in., square ft., and improvised units).

782890954A354519B3C6E311FB432A3F.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

337DDCEB8F044ED586A63819E36C5EA9.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

D3F070E37973485691366959494183B6.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concept of area measurement.

09964B7B7EF748F59D68435CA2CF9644.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

EC93CFADE1FD475EBF66F581CD716A78.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units – whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

3AC5EB0916CF49528C31E88541432694.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how may less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

2BF0458BF9594D09BC818E252608CE4B.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

41851697E84D4CC092B9894704BD149B.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

20008C8752D247A9B4A5ABE48EA444B8.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

96F6C0DC466D42249D4CFFDCA22A25DE.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

EC258515954A40E4A9B3359E59CFE26E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

4C2499F21D8F4DE78554E7C9E2AD50D4.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model

429154862B6D47C9AAD9719363C6E8BF.description: Represent two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on the number line.

F7377F1D10644DC784110DB5A758CE14.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

F7AE5617B9BC4AB29180B9F8B7FFEC7B.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths of 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

B76DF049331045D1BA2BC7F1F1AE44C9.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

023407FE44CA445B8645143C5FF09949.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

5272128F98F7456D8277C071956639E1.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

641AD01CDE00467B809A19635D87E192.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

F6765D4253EB4976A2FCD1BAC980DDD4.description: Number And Operations-Fractions (Limited To Fractions With Denominators 2,3,4,6,8)

42ADEE1334D14CAC9FA2D6DCC83AB4C6.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range of 10-90 (e.g., 9 x 80, 5 x 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

31A31ADBBAF14057A248ED54C0826F61.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

F5C9BAB431E14368A2F81E99108D55C8.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

2141D0646CCA41149D242C2A818AFDD4.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

64BCDA9FE4DD48F48C52F956C4F69EF0.description: Number And Operations In Base Ten

72776AA309324198B55CF654A4A01909.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

BDAAB350E4604972AF24DF84FB8F0776.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

C0062BAABA37426791DD78699304FEA0.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

F2876C782CF34F9EB6F4B219E2F6BE5C.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 x 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

50E1D3FAC87A4DBA976ABCA7AEFED56F.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

7348A2121DE24972B557A294D884BB67.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
  • If 6 x 4 = 24 is known, then 4 x 6 = 24 is also known. (Commutative property of multiplication)
  • 3 x 5 x 2 can be found by 3 x 5 = 15, then 15 x 2 = 30, or by 5 x 2 = 10, then 3 x 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication)
  • Knowing that 8 x 5 = 40 and 8 x 2 = 16, one can find 8 x 7 as 8 x (5 + 2) = (8 x 5) + (8 x 2) which leads to 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property)

0A4A5F994FE84B188C913B1ED96C1882.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

A7D58F28F16A4F769CAC0AD2EAA60807.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

3C4D820B74EB4C32A8AAC28AB5254A0C.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

F1559F2E982D4022BDB1AB269EC23A2A.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

A33E1C0D8F314EB6A5949F25B39C7FBA.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 x 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.

8DF541D2A32E44B1A176F44F04ECD9A1.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 2

B17383A82B9B4D2284F785F8BA89A108.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

011F2B63F78140ED9A324957300AC039.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

6F4D2F2590B84A5F9A55A2DE5C06194F.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specific attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

05157B3B2A9E42A99BE732A30FA67997.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

C129C65E44EB4CF8B9417F876D722D80.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

DD4A824E3F1C4FDBAFB5CE0B87C7DA9B.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

C83CD8D76AB542A3B6449C5BD4394756.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

76F0038371274470B2CCE3A17EB48F79.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

C8EC12062121400181AB4B54E4375932.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the number 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

443808D62BFA491DB66F3F52C191FA29.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

AB814CD88C1A4080AFDE44E7EFDE54CD.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

BB424C941AEE4ACDAD72B760AAB98C86.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

F19AEC172ED64D3EBC9B6D86E88BCFE7.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

BEE02743BCD14466A403B3E76B71BBC5.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

E6476E6BF95646E5BA46687001BDD33D.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

1938E8E1DCCA4FDEBBBA8C540D81E9AB.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

285644A8090D4A07B22F763F70CC6205.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.

6F8FA34CEBFC4C0C9FCA29FFB5985C84.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100-900.

4B93627DD0814EA4B7FE88643CB546E6.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

3403C4E2C60D44A68C6436F99BB5AF66.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value, properties of operations.

8EF245AB6A624DC4B1CFC5E1D953BFA6.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

F44A0AE4A72346BD82B40355F9BE2878.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

E51B0AED43D8414BB1DEBCC731CC5EB0.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

B24CB250B6F242EF95FBC5ED4EC2F269.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

21AA5BE803A245B5AE9614C14A4A8F72.description: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

705C9410B907479F8FB2DD80701B311E.description: Understand the following as a special case: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens -- called a "hundred."

8A9345203E884484B636C5D7C0ABF4C5.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones.

6068C1C6881D4DC2A5FAC5DBF3F31B1E.description: Number And Operations In Base Ten

334D7B914CAB4B74B2236AB114CBC233.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

B24410C5E8F94AD19B8AB388F731EF3A.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20 has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

8A2111470AE047779711FB87D18F96BF.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

23409652ACF741FE9BC1A75051DC3059.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

E81045CA7720437DB4B22FAB89134E04.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

78821E52187240D9A4CA6EFBDA7D6D1F.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 4

02005657897548778DB13FB211A1D4AB.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

8E0639EA3AF64DB4AB5FD0F61708728A.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

A4BEB572DEF4491D952EAFBCEAB449C2.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

0672884A69444948AE602330D960DFED.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shape by properties of their lines and angles.

BD7CA8D6EC994B5E81E5576197DE47C6.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

63F7912E60374C2BB1A021F619314C4B.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

32FAABBBEBEB4F1899E6DA9812700ADC.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

3BCA621407964B4F9D6789D6F4CC05D5.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of the circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

3F1D0A57908340728C32874119EBB49F.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.

0B11034713F141F99FEE216A0931A6ED.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts or angle and measure angles.

077FA9502FCA4DDFA1A963023EF9EB30.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

8DD4C0225CC44F7A9AF9E1374D13FA08.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems. For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formulas as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

FE4A6104B4F340D985CF5884F86FBC45.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

E9CA21B160EC439A96BB1DB8DAE7DB6E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm, kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

879165E549354822A9BE67D76F7EA5E7.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements for a larger unit to a smaller unit.

ED8582697C5B4215AEA886811D0B615C.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

0C5403EFCA2440EC8E20559061A7193F.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 and 100.

765C1ED50ED143409AD76D0322CC57C8.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

0B7FE41C9F3749A9AB6B2EC958F4F38F.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

A2603771D4484D03BFBD0C6EBF0E9F95.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

CE5F4BA4DDE24CF78FD324AA00200BCE.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

5CCDD039F3CD4897BE444D0462E64854.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

6EA302D830D842BAA21515B3A759BE57.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

AF81124F24404244B8D5DB10F292F253.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

8D534970249E4275BCAABB7F5378D566.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

570AF7576F764064AE318A86154A6A7F.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition as an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

9A66FDF81D8A48D7A4CFDA803C339215.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

0463175A3E6C45C286338DFBCC3E249A.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a >1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

16D6DAA22CC345A2A0619ACB2506CAB2.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

0B2C3C6165B1444F98875BF3207B344E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

597B125E62B0477EAAA793EA5451E9EE.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n x a)/(n x b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

86186EBA903243AFA0C492EFDD6E4F73.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

AAB66EA0C2044000BD38390B265C1FEA.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

128848C2B12345ADB283A8B61D4A67F1.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two- digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

B5A343D0B99B41CA8E8B9EDF74C373D3.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

02D180C83F994F8F9E8E998677060BBF.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

3D21B968A26F4AE2B1835215504F3C05.description: Use place value understanding to round multi- digit whole numbers to any place.

7ABB536320DD4F2FA36E32F43A2974EE.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

98DE54D0BE7B433A8E83753259AAC002.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

4A3F21BB88084790BC9CA1CEE6D24AAA.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

90E1D764E666478B8FFB86731989E9B9.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

FA15E5CC50194FA8B4C7CB095D0B65A4.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100.Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1- 100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range of 1-100 is prime or composite.

4319A9D42E784A388716053E34F46D4D.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

0BC25EDCFC9A48FF9BE102F74C0BBD9A.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

25CB85D62EE142858CF54B8F7EA3D1C0.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

1F95F4DA2A77499F914508C6D03AC7EF.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 x 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

616E8C360E4E4B608D89EA435F86764F.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 1

4C0799CE93D34A1282A818140D39497D.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

8B40BBC1D7D84B1392A05EDE99065895.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

1CC19C2B6C1A4A1F9E3A8C7DB80ABA80.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

41CF2F1D3F3D4452A9328A232ADA56B4.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

F21BB469DB864BDB851EBFF459E3D92E.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

DAF0F833E90F4602B845C986CCFF59B0.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

0BD62ECA5DCF439A8C1E3B530F355330.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

7AE892E8A3DB410291FB4A5060126F9D.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length unit.

4EDE1E45F93542AF8DE898CEF4F2218F.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range of 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range of 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

8BB44549BA71432DAE8DF22AEE2E194B.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

E24481EF280941E793D9DBBF885F3626.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones, and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

815131DE5C064E8BA6A13069B4989263.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

1CB14A5FF92346F68CBC04C60AD0E9CB.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

2E2EE1EB43954168A0246F994486723C.description: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

2CEB8C6E4B684CEB95E309B47CEF6BC6.description: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

73D9E1D189D44CDEABBA041CAE6D107F.description: Understand the following as a special case: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones -- called a "ten."

E464308EB65C4D5585863578F68C7116.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.

23AB3DBE26464358A182CC07E4321D0A.description: Count to 120 starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

75BB446A224E483ABD32DD84BAE5E5BE.description: Number And Operations In Base Ten

9D86876C4D774090A186B909F5D1E558.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.

9A2C0516CDC84E5D8DBF838609A772DE.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.

31F4C8C215E74079BE21BF085B4715AA.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

CD2BBA503AF54608BF4BD44C9EE5FCF5.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on, making ten (e.g. 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4, which leads to 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1, which leads to 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1, which equals 13).

4A306785640B46EE87DDE17205B98A5D.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

0FAB7B3F80A140158FC874F5CAADDC74.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

B487C0E762D34C1290DA075A88B295B1.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. (Students need not use formal terms for these properties.)

6724A126E2A145969705454D0AD6845C.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and relationship between addition and subtraction.

23790C3557034D698CEBE617714EF43B.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

CC13A720858F4507A7DE2D10E4BDA9DB.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

9A7B6803CEA345DA8BC01519D0EF1CB1.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Kindergarten

5187B92FA294418E9A5D48CCC152E452.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.

7ECAE689384D4C99AE6C6879AFE9B4D0.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

4F14B52EE53B4D1F834C3053DF3D60DE.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

8571835A6C0A4A3D9C5E6FEA10DCE9EA.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shape.

5BBF239E855640378E7BA07196F56088.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

8A2C6B61716B4AEABA545327D2817BBB.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

AA71D6E8810D4C819C8D8760C9D14CA0.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

CC0AB95ADAE041E6972B8B6E5A20B0E7.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

CAD5220AEED645B1ADBE0EA70E42F177.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the number of objects in each category and sort the categories by count. (Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.).

46C00194E8154332BA5706C48A3A23A3.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

BB867D04B2D64CE0A449117D7BD640DE.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

52D8C3AE0B9149E1B3B83BD088009C49.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

A8EC811571904402AAE38FC68F44C04C.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (such as 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

AD261054D10C4309A27826D38AED222C.description: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.

16F6E2736BF94B08AFAD71A708B09C87.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

7D73F7ABEBC2416E832BC3A7209ADD50.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawing, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

10DCFBB060084011A75C46A04BF777C4.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

8DB3E33FB38445119E5296229C23A54C.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, or verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

3A496119D448490DB18D8DA1110E8E3E.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

355916D400BD4140B8A13F9416B0EFEE.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

FA0272E81386455B9B42B2EB2BC01B2D.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies (Include groups with up to ten objects).

E27D7A0110714A1B9837AB2B0332BD6E.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.

13E68D9F0E054039BBC6EF905BDD27B9.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

6B543099AEEF4669AD1FB7D7CAA3C15B.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

4D25735EC0784725BE3A529B3F391207.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

FB50B45E105B4110AA64D720B28766CE.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

F3D685BF2C7341EBB28A7DF2EBCF22E4.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

499F9BAF669643BB9DFE6EFCC429CBC6.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

DE7A036FF5A14D68B974B8CBB72C8FC4.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

4E2A3BDE0BF343B88FE89DFEE0B9677E.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

8F982DE9B47A4DA8A46F4629A0C0156D.description: Know number names and the count sequence.
