document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Pre-Kindergarten

5A959958C0DB4061B3FCA764EEB4EA49.description: Compose and describe structures using three-dimensional shapes. Descriptions may include shape attributes, relative position, etc.

62AD30EA1CDE4953AE74B09AAEB86023.description: Use real world examples to describe three-dimensional objects using correct mathematical vocabulary (cube, sphere, and cylinder).

64DEBE097EDC465DB3978CDBC6322BE8.description: Work with three- dimensional shapes to gain foundations for geometric thinking.

B4D5FA07751B43B2A01B4B685B3DAAFB.description: Group the shapes by like attributes and distinguish between examples and non-examples of various two-dimensional shapes.

DD1AD15D69E847ABA8577FCED13F01E3.description: Match like two-dimensional shapes and correctly name the shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

7AC6C819EBCA4599977E2F6F8DF4D3E8.description: Identify and describe two dimensional shapes (circles, triangles, rectangles, including a square which is a special rectangle).

7FD89FAE599F4AF69C472222E2BAEAD3.description: Compare categories using words such as greater than/more, less than, and equal to/same.

92164E2A29ED46EC8302DE9B49FC4D6C.description: Sort objects into given categories and self-selected categories. Identify the attribute by which the objects were sorted.

3D615CA8BBE84C0EA73ECD9A4F9E565A.description: Sort objects into categories and compare quantities.

40D75BAE474F4312928DEF00CB504B7F.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, using words such as "bigger/smaller," "longer/shorter," "lighter/heavier," or "taller/shorter". Order up to 3 objects by a measureable attribute (e.g. biggest to smallest).

05565FDA5D26466C9D7A637E1277AB63.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight.

7FF28AD405AA4E3E805DA44FAF6EC033.description: For any quantity 1-5, use objects or drawings to find the quantity that must be added to make 5.

D0726E9BED42430DBBBE279536E0DF9E.description: Decompose a quantity, less than or equal to 5, then to 10, into pairs in more than one way, e.g. by using objects or drawings.

81738FAABBED4C50A72C786AD3609A70.description: Represent simple addition and subtraction problems with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps),acting out situations, or verbal explanations, up to 5.

BCC300D66DE144F1BD5192A142176D81.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

A948445B1CC442248699C7659D4815B5.description: Compare groups of objects up to 5 and then to 10. Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies (includes groups with up to 5 objects).

A3E99AA8F1754A068D2B51F90F4FBBD8.description: Represent a number by producing sets of objects with concrete materials, pictures, and or numerals. (First 0-5 and then to 10). Can correctly respond when asked "how many" after counting concrete objects.

8ECA805620EE4BC7BFC9F4EA6FD7736F.description: Begin to recognize that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

27A819948F7241CA9B068EC8E8A991AF.description: Recognize that the last number name said, tells the number of objects counted. Recognize the count remains the same regardless of the order or arrangement of the objects.

0127071D153B4D2B8E05572372B0472D.description: When counting objects 1-10, say the number names in standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name.

4156137A10EE4D77B6D4652D26F2B4C6.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities to 5, then to 10; connect counting to cardinality.

980D233B9C6F4AF09D9D23FD66C53478.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

3396D4BE074B4A3FA01B6A8848E2A1CE.description: Recognize the number of objects in a set without counting (subitizing) using 1-5 objects. Use 1-3 objects of irregular or unfamiliar patterns and 4 or 5 objects with familiar patterns.

2F0E766D85744DC6ACCEAF8EBF9FE6EC.description: Identify which number comes just after or just before a given number in the counting sequence to 10 with visual supports and manipulatives.

99374369732941E08588394B9050F238.description: Verbally count to 10 by ones and then develop rote counting to 20 by ones.

DFFBE6DCE09444BD958B6C9D0153D204.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 8

B8ADF400E49A48AD9095CEAAB4AF3A50.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

4CFCD9E7C79B41C1A6F6B1A4E4966B2D.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

C38A245D3F034D4FA2D9CC3371BFB1CC.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

8745A095D9CD4CDEAD482318C159F89B.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

298AE92D1F49466685FE751B70E7495E.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

79487744E79F430381EA6FFA3F4368A9.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

21E70DC906A546249BF46407A38EEDBF.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

AD0649813B0149EFA67390612CC2151F.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

CD94B64315024C9DB6F8AFCBBFCC6715.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

E7423ABE621A4DCA96246FB90E84A907.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

236A91B137144A7EAECA4237D1312865.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle- angle criterion for similarity of triangles.

7C8C5BFA6CF941788DF2E37E33A1C01E.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

92EAD5AD7C39427EA12C3286A2B8CDF0.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

65F249BC31A3483DBD9518D4E8DBE4EA.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

C2EA6081B2C3436FB970E9B2EE866451.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

82DE1FA31B194686A767D24653906F6A.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

D93DA270778542BB9591864F5DA6F21B.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

F9B7556F23C349358EB05B07E21B9137.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations.

E50F09E6554C48E4B84B19FB673BE7CB.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

F5826085996C4BC79598AD76F0A87C9C.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

76CC684187E04239AB5FB86792E880BB.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

477D80CB2E104FF8B945238AFD69DA9D.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

E494BF1AD31B4D0AA61FB2DD4C6B938F.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

D9891E77BCC34D9C9F5042DD77F31043.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

D8B3C98D12C24F5A923FC5B2B1A069D0.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output (function notation is not required in Grade 8).

67757285355E46A2850CB04BEE65FAC0.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

00AFFA1D8C7E4DB8A4F20450A56A63FB.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

F1E2FF24136D4899858047C0A6EC5B15.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

E539AE0188D849EAB9E09ADCD1EDF9F1.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

F0C626482C76404FBD3AA8EFB090131C.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (a and b are different numbers).

AB0C8327D6DF4585BDD16F94D7D2C1AF.description: Solve linear equations in one variable

3D83D82BBFC84D74B9C606B3343E8E53.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

DFF664FF55AD4FC9B7DCE918B7D75593.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y=mx for a line through the origin, and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

CE413E64522F4C97B73A2D7D3C6A7656.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

FAE8D61B6D5E42AAA9AEC7C499F58B25.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

6D4F5069D052435095954B1BBE1B0B25.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

55031039F9CB46509087C2F1BFF5E60B.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

EBC858DF98E7416D8F0FFF14CE6C389F.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

C6C7B96F83AB43B6AF7282F7F21136A2.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

94692326CBF844F2BCFA039C1960148D.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

33612ACE91F647DDA5164556F2F8CE09.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

40A61EE8A82E43E996DD4198FB7C0638.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

638EF3B67A9E4688961CE92DB8E6DF4C.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 6

5DF1B230089949ED9641EA0A26A7B154.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data was gathered.

193C78B0E35A47388AA4010BC794DF77.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data was gathered.

E33E008068E04107929E257D362ACF56.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

1806B1CB19B14BAB9A18A0506B2ADCD7.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

F00F96BCCC0E49B19F4E29B7B8F245CC.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

E6E5D41D48CA479F83C5A181ECCAB826.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

5776A8B90A384DA98916FEABA4A1D7A6.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

9C83D0C79A674916B6E4B562A629CBBC.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

4C81D20165F64CB7BC6129DF57578898.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

F3F6A6DD379F45429C1713AB4AF9A2D9.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

0BE0AFD1EC7E440386BD0DD4A2C2C8CA.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = lwh and V = Bh to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

C08B2ECD4C3D4853A7D62D23E5A13376.description: Find area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

0887FE6B5BF24D79A9590577D3523404.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

DBCE884E0F9349FA80A6F504157FC7CB.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

BC25577FD431434FB0F977B04A0F37DE.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

09EB6B83F59C40BFA21D5F2A26397C90.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < chave infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

2A63C1BF701348BA9C0B54D527F7D10B.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x +p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

BE00074695E7476789D763AE6283B526.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

D52F78559D8047C095E651A4FCC4903E.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true

1824F33FD0A24810A1C7E539A331B1CD.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

0C4050D58FA54ADFA25EDA89577488B1.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).

A46DF1F48ABE434A886419350197BA7B.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

3A5F60BE8F47440DA003B4BB9BA8C09C.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values for their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

4FF8B06C1FC2441A9FAA2D2FF4FBD531.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

4F09B040B8324B86991713CF327C0006.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

5ABFAA9A621E4CB3BDEE027D0D5868B3.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

1B86B814A58A4C27B8E8D5601BB45B4E.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

F20FA747D80449D591BD4257D794FEED.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

FC08853B45734F66801934FD4346E400.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all 4 quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with same first coordinate or same second coordinate.

754E0D38671F49C3AFF6182D6DC74E53.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

34522B036AD64C298BAA0EB47E3A34C5.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

FE9F771A47E84EA0B4CA4961BF0C7F61.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

D0061BF5434848219BB22E68A33877C3.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

772B55AC3EB14AF2BE15E9181E3D7EBA.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

CE1D7016C550440FBD75C8904DD72E3E.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

441E002C14274CAF9E559626D39C9746.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

13DC7020099E4BE7B8C10D6601480F50.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

BDCFB1C4F32245B49875C5803CD6EE40.description: Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

0D70885849BE43F394C8C60F32196E4E.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, debits/credits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

6AD234D48354493E9ED9249A79956D57.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

F2DB3DA6D72647DC90B4802545848ABB.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

81D33E7E596C434880102C6BD709B7B8.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

8D54B40B82A945809839AB6E331C4D5A.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

88752F42E62B42578123B587BD676BD5.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

074A2B1C60454199852FE82400A74327.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

390A9683D11E46A6B5F6B678BD2BB729.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

F3DF8ED35B1D4385A4C4EFF9F68448D0.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

581FF314682D4AD9A1D576C4AF119026.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole given a part and the percent.

020DC55B41244E858D2D72D4435E55CD.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

BA4E01DBAC8A4F72A495E928E9DB0FE5.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

0721BC4F2E9845C3BC43E33FCB111F56.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

4C7A2DC43B5245078A6D875609EC211B.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0 (b not equal to zero), and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

A053CB035C13465E8AEF4AD75565A597.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

4307C67480D24456AFD6D25CCE91DC43.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Mathematics Curriculum Framework - Grade 7

EDF2B08631E8417DB0D406977F8B5C07.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

90554B5099B5486284003A0E7E8D5C46.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

0792875802BF4D19ACF05B6B0F949F84.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

1B8723F3A6BC4AACB59CA369C754E5DF.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

7B7A5C4EEC694D498683063326CB4BE9.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

9EA4107797D84C75978F63FB7064098A.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

9835D3F4902442DDB77876EEB1804D11.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events; compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; and if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

400AEA81BCE24F89BE56F4E234C9F626.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

2401C6B613FB4AF4AE0E9F302D7272B8.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

64F137FA0681440996BB7A57BE6F2FB1.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

D1EDE5EEFFD94D8AB215E7EA479DE838.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

419F89EE54E1400FA62128193DFDA5B7.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

C4A5329C75E045629DCA6F0179BF9A40.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

2CF62972BC5B431B9DAA7F7A5F48FA58.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

ABA01719D4CD4D1B8ABDA0B39EC9290E.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

1012BC181D7743609D2F4A4FCA62BA7C.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

8AE9FDA8BBBD48FB8920D102C63CFC9F.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

4EAD785E69A64D92B0CE3F867A991654.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

75834414962343D2ACF43398CCAE9EEC.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

E5C604FB17E34BCC8066080ADAE85412.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

50D2B8A966214F6CB7612BDBBA03488F.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures resulting from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

67500600DF184B7DA096E8A11D3781D3.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing (drawing?) triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

3C61E740874A4953A87CB127FAFBA37B.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

4C6D8492BA884DBBA40CE7F484F66436.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

FE0AF585D66941F89644A6D1E3542FB2.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers; graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

9CC4E917BAF44674A4FD15CD54D14144.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers; solve equations of these forms fluently; compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

3149011632E44B5C95ACE421BBBE1B52.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

A5E3C039E5D1435A842A326ED3C7B648.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically; apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

68E1B165EC9A4BDC8FB0F01AEB339B0C.description: Solve real-life mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

BB729E27109749F1816288F5DA7424E8.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

91D14BE763DC414CB606DCEF90D9B140.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

C1309A35DF884D8DA450F0F428C0BDDE.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

B12EAAEDF1BB47D2ACB296279FA8543C.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

8FE1D4351CE549F3A9C2E1D31872FF1C.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; and know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

BC2E9839893F4697B7877E2A035FDB1E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

D81DE7E189C74666BEC6337A997C2AB6.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -(p/q) = -p/q = p/-q. Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

A2379FC6A5854B57BA2332BA1136DA5D.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1)= 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

ACFF4EE7F25345449FDA8E2D74F07C82.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational number.

26F121DEA5E0465680A0C0BA4E449591.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

1C17BC47C91341E3BD7E66583C89F868.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

77216F04B82E47D9A9059E59AF78FAA6.description: Understand p +q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

CBC5260DB8874E3DAD55189B80767C96.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.

FBE120EF0C4440FE9DF715AF179FE823.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, and represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

F970F209F0B8411DB8DB1D30AB5E1F36.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

31A24CAAF0104B97920E2547BF358A68.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.

887678A81EC7444D8F7F23B3F970D1DF.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

660643EB9468423CBA0719CF469BA04F.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

E75374C1276C4FA5967A98A7536725A8.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

985190BD59754C03B6F17D350D605F81.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

63F4EC556BBF41AE8B3F762BC33410B0.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like and or different units.

30A08FD74A0E48499E93C1EF16D1AD76.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

smallest).

Begin to recognize that each successive number name refers to a quantity
that is one larger.

Recognize that the last number name said tells the number of objects
counted. Recognize the count remains the same regardless of the order or
arrangement of the objects.

pairing each object with one and only one number name.

Refer to details and examples in a text
when explaining what the text says explicitly
and when drawing inferences from the text.

5D069C40383F4720A9137929202E68C6.description:
By the end of the year, read and
comprehend literature, including stories,
dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text
complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding
as needed at the high end of the range.

B8FD449E4D6641FC93BEB3D853E65E36.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

389458977FE3466C85E06C5080B5B6DF.description:
Compare and contrast the treatment of
similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of
good and evil) and patterns of events(e.g., the
quest) in stories, myths, and traditional
literature from different cultures.

3B53A88EA904461384D049B007583320.description:
Make connections between the text of a
story or drama and a visual or oral
presentation of the text, identifying where
each version reflects specific descriptions and
directions in the text.

61204CC3CC184F47A89935342EC77DA5.description:
Compare and contrast the point of view
from which different stories are narrated,
including the difference between first- and
third-person narrations.

8FED8427D0C845F9903B53E81B9E516C.description:
Explain major differences between
poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the
structural elements of poems (e.g., verse,
rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of
characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue,
stage directions) when writing or speaking
about a text.

3DE7F0F8817549579DB2B3CA47B71639.description:
Determine the meaning of words and
phrases as they are used in a text, including
those that allude to significant characters
found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).

F87F2B756E634F32B4DAB1575F78F9E8.description:
Describe in depth a character, setting, or
event in a story or drama, drawing on specific
details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts,
words, or actions).

726AFCFB140B47539EF14DBECFB163AE.description:
Determine a theme of a story, drama, or
poem from details in the text; summarize the
text.

8782B8B3D275474FA465F257FF68135C.description:
Refer to details and examples in a text
when explaining what the text says explicitly
and when drawing inferences from the text.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Standards for English Language Arts Grades 3-5

F6650B9FCD3448CC9E44802502E457A5.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade
appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those
that signal contrast, addition, and other logical
relationships (e.g., however, although,
nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

7CF60FF97E5B45B8A7D476B95E307614.description:
Use the relationship between
particular words (e.g., synonyms,
antonyms, homographs) to better
understand each of the words.

FCC22B9F46DA4FC7AEFF80B6DFBF6136.description:
Recognize and explain the meaning
of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

3052250341944012BFCD81C539881849.description:
Interpret figurative language,
including similes and metaphors, in
context.

8A1332C8C97842A6BAB8C9EA4F51B592.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative
language, word relationships, and nuances in
word meanings.

3656722520764FD9B135FA3CB6E6A7B9.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g.,
dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both
print and digital, to find the pronunciation
and determine or clarify the precise
meaning of key words and phrases.

8EC15E46C96141E2B06A88C42C9EF12A.description:
Use common, grade appropriate
Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues
to the meaning of a word (e.g.,
photograph, photosynthesis).

9A9969EE06504C8CBC1B0C1E42A20C19.description:
Use context (e.g., cause/effect
relationships and comparisons in text) as a
clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

09038001E73047EEA11E0F2016146176.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of
unknown and multiple-meaning words and
phrases based on grade 5 reading and content,
choosing flexibly from a range of strategies. 

65A8B8F57E6B44B4AF8A0DE89F0F3D77.description:
Compare and contrast the varieties
of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in
stories, dramas, or poems.

7E5390F1D93F4B998D5D91EE1CF46571.description:
Expand, combine, and reduce
sentences for meaning, reader/listener
interest, and style.

BCDDCCCD566D42758571F70166999115.description:
Use knowledge of language and its
conventions when writing, speaking, reading,
or listening.

B7B2BA55ED724348B5268A7F522B727A.description:
Spell grade-appropriate words
correctly, consulting references as needed.

DE3882EF22344F558E37AD41E50B9932.description:
Use underlining, quotation marks,
or italics to indicate titles of works.

0380A702DF344818BCCAAED57E7A5319.description:
Use a comma to set off the words
yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off
a tag question from the rest of the
sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to
indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you,
Steve?).

69BE2AE002BE4AA58E504DD9EE4A73AB.description:
Use a comma to separate an
introductory element from the rest of the
sentence.

131D689C48C34E22BB818886970C06B3.description:
Use punctuation to separate items
in a series. *

1E5B8DEA15374A7698A53833972FB09C.description:
Demonstrate command of the
conventions of standard English capitalization,
punctuation, and spelling when writing.

C675AA156B174BE2A8E1ABE4737B451E.description:
Recognize and correct
inappropriate shifts in verb tense. *

435DC71AF3CE45A1A0D87E1E29C8B7BE.description:
Use verb tense to convey various
times, sequences, states, and conditions.

B42716956010431D8CBF7ECDD994E575.description:
Form and use the perfect (e.g., I
had walked; I have walked; I will have
walked) verb tenses.

DB086E01065F4F788A7C9FDDD1C7C813.description:
Explain the function of
conjunctions, prepositions, and
interjections in general and their function
in particular sentences.

8CD34CA9BA074DECA29B54AE8E1760A6.description:
Demonstrate command of the
conventions of standard English grammar and
usage when writing or speaking.

E999F8DDF34B4217B172734987688502.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts
and tasks, using formal English when
appropriate to task and situation (See grade 5
Language standards 1 and 3 for specific
expectations.)

1F4A72C8FCE147D8A41524099EE8B076.description:
Include multimedia components(e.g.,
graphics, sound) and visual displays in
presentations when appropriate to enhance
the development of main ideas or themes.

17331CDEE5DD4FB6B555BA9EF8C1D3E2.description:
Report on a topic or text or present an
opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using
appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive
details to support main ideas or themes; speak
clearly at an understandable pace.

31583A61CA034FF8A10219E7E8CF6169.description:
Summarize the points a speaker makes
and explain how each claim is supported by
reasons and evidence.

395F0999DF3646419F0A5D50398935F9.description:
Summarize a written text read aloud or
information presented in diverse media and
formats, including visually, quantitatively, and
orally.

F57A938589B842CD94065553AECDFBAB.description:
Review the key ideas expressed
and draw conclusions in light of
information and knowledge gained from
the discussions.

9D1EDD2BAFB0408C8A7D59096B492BFD.description:
Pose and respond to specific
questions by making comments that
contribute to the discussion and elaborate
on the remarks of others.

21292B5910CF4722B103CAEA489EF1CD.description:
Follow agreed-upon rules for
discussions and carry out assigned roles.

A347A76E60004994B9D9AE21E960D254.description:
Come to discussions prepared,
having read or studied required material;
explicitly draw on that preparation and
other information known about the topic
to explore ideas under discussion.

4612717A3A01445084EB47DE4A66FD98.description:
Engage effectively in a range of
collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in
groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners
on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others'
ideas and expressing their own clearly.

FEE814D870B44AE184A414033F5CDF24.description:
Write routinely over extended time
frames (time for research, reflection, and
revision) and shorter time frames (a single
sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

AC40893847464933BD8818A2F86C3399.description:
Apply grade 5 Reading standards
to informational texts(e.g., "Explain how
an author uses reasons and evidence to
support particular points in a text,
identifying which reasons and evidence
support which point[s]"").

2F9FB48A2F4E451685D395DC8118AD9A.description:
Apply grade 5 Reading standards
to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast
two or more characters, settings, or events
in a story or a drama, drawing on specific
details in the text [e.g., how characters
interact]").

9404AE691D534F18AC3160E0943F278D.description:
Draw evidence from literary or
informational texts to support analysis,
reflection, and research.

732FEEB5A69D4049BB595BB1AB5C769B.description:
Recall relevant information from
experiences or gather relevant information
from print and digital sources; summarize or
paraphrase information in notes and finished
work, and provide a list of sources.

91C968A5C8854BD3BBB128870A284DA2.description:
Conduct short research projects that use
several sources to build knowledge through
investigation of different aspects of a topic.

33D1D9A056074DAA8C3A08461016D78D.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

027554ED5AD14479B2FEF7CCFACB3530.description:
With some guidance and support from
adults, use technology, including the Internet,
to produce and publish writing as well as to
interact and collaborate with others;
demonstrate sufficient command of
keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two
pages in a single sitting.

44C3E679E2EA4BAD9A8CDD8437E1ABE9.description:
With guidance and support from peers
and adults, develop and strengthen writing as
needed by planning, revising, editing,
rewriting, or trying a new approach. (Editing
for conventions should demonstrate command
of Language standards 1-3 up to and including
grade 5.)

53ED396DE15D402BAD6A60A6BBF93021.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in
which the development and organization are
appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
(Grade-specific expectations for writing types
are defined in standards 1-3 above.)

C58F2A304A8942E4BB3F4C25F0EEB4C4.description:
Provide a conclusion that follows
from the narrated experiences or events.

D38B6D7505BF49ADAC43017A1802DE18.description:
Use concrete words and phrases
and sensory details to convey experiences
and events precisely.

A534EFF6655D4588BAF295719F71AEBB.description:
Use a variety of transitional
words, phrases, and clauses to manage the
sequence of events.

6BC3E3479F584F978B47F0FA2F8286E4.description:
Use narrative techniques, such as
dialogue, description, and pacing, to
develop experiences and events or show
the responses of characters to situations.

51E098A8DBC34F06BA57AD52EC149604.description:
Orient the reader by establishing
a situation and introducing a narrator
and/or characters; organize an event
sequence that unfolds naturally.

4ACCD2D1B0AC4048AE3ED05D04B0F808.description:
Write narratives to develop real or
imagined experiences or events using effective
technique, descriptive details, and clear event
sequences.

0158E1622F484C999257482B6EDB7494.description:
Provide a concluding statement or
section related to the information or
explanation presented.

2612125438014507AB2286769A63D674.description:
Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or
explain the topic.

799FCC1D53C24F719270EBDECA5B04BA.description:
Link ideas within and across
categories of information using words,
phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast,
especially).

F58ACF4A691B4B4F9312727405F1B0CA.description:
Develop the topic with facts,
definitions, concrete details, quotations,
or other information and examples related
to the topic.

E660CA6313DD420F912C862D974606D0.description:
Introduce a topic clearly, provide
a general observation and focus, and
group related information logically;
include formatting (e.g., headings),
illustrations, and multimedia when useful
to aiding comprehension.

8B2BBC2EED98474BA443A3E90A3D865A.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts to
examine a topic and convey ideas and
information clearly.

12DCA96CBE5043979C783BF7BEA14438.description:
Provide a concluding statement or
section related to the opinion presented.

F0D08E7A7A1C469086017894D3513B87.description:
Link opinion and reasons using
words, phrases, and clauses (e.g.,
consequently, specifically).

9401E958F20045F48808377A9341B51B.description:
Provide logically ordered reasons
that are supported by facts and details.

9A3C839B443B43EA8EF5FC1FE1F7DA89.description:
Introduce a topic or text clearly,
state an opinion, and create an
organizational structure in which ideas are
logically grouped to support the writer's
purpose.

5826424363274956953553D2BEF9337F.description:
Write opinion pieces on topics or texts,
supporting a point of view with reasons and
information.

18E7869936FF471283C985D8B0B791A5.description:
Use context to confirm or self correct word recognition and
understanding, rereading as necessary.

614E7633EAA24A1E829C33317EE0830F.description:
Read grade-level prose and
poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate
rate, and expression on successive
readings.

D0D931322F19416F9E23C70221C2514F.description:
Read grade-level text with
purpose and understanding.

FF3AF0CDDD6B4D86B8C1DE58DF13F437.description:
Read with sufficient accuracy and
fluency to support comprehension.

47D4A36F11CB4D03AD04A4F50E54F382.description:
Use combined knowledge of all
letter-sound correspondences,
syllabication patterns, and morphology
(e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately
unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context
and out of context.

3B79F590DC6C4600B00A671E88938858.description:
Know and apply grade-level phonics and word
analysis skills in decoding words.

A1495261C3F643DD9ED0AFFDF7EDEE6A.description:
By the end of the year, read and
comprehend informational texts, including
history/social studies, science, and technical
texts, at the high end of the grades 4-5 text
complexity band independently and
proficiently.

D0A993AF7B7E43B0B0E36966BFA89816.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

119B1D2FEDA44D30AC8D9742788F8516.description:
Integrate information from several texts
on the same topic in order to write or speak
about the subject knowledgeably.

207DE47BF1774939BF484C5107C4644F.description:
Explain how an author uses reasons and
evidence to support particular points in a text,
identifying which reasons and evidence
support which point(s).

609D0C07CF1C47159877145FA0CDF3B5.description:
Draw on information from multiple print
or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to
locate an answer to a question quickly or to
solve a problem efficiently.

EC431D6C2EF0484091CB42118C4FC62E.description:
Analyze multiple accounts of the same
event or topic, noting important similarities
and differences in the point of view they
represent.

7AB98AC2C6264F06B01B01B1F277B1B0.description:
Compare and contrast the overall
structure (e.g., chronology, comparison,
cause/effect, problem/solution) of events,
ideas, concepts, or information in two or more
texts.

D21C6FFB541549DD94DC8D23B1DA2BD9.description:
Determine the meaning of general
academic and domain-specific words and
phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or
subject area.

41BD8C3750474DC891365305873FDB49.description:
Explain the relationships or interactions
between two or more individuals, events,
ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or
technical text based on specific information in
the text.

1C0B6015E78E4C8E9A4FF80A7907B0D3.description:
Determine two or more main ideas of a
text and explain how they are supported by
key details; summarize the text.

6A4DA8CE30784595AB0E1B64268C562D.description:
Quote accurately from a text when
explaining what the text says explicitly and
when drawing inferences from the text.

45EC80D6B2DA4C71A1DBAF362DCB6949.description:
By the end of the year, read and
comprehend literature, including stories,
dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the
grades 4-5 text complexity band independently
and proficiently.

222BB33D062F40FA8852F9CDE8D0470B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

0906D4E2790C4DA9AA094BAA47BEFAB4.description:
Compare and contrast stories in the
same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure
stories) on their approaches to similar themes
and topics.

4146BFF734A5407EBC065868791B00DF.description:
Analyze how visual and multimedia
elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or
beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel,
multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale,
myth, poem).

E8407C62973B45AC92DB6F1302D44B49.description:
Describe how a narrator's or speaker's
point of view influences how events are
described.

DD1637D98AE54A88BC1F3CB740261CFB.description:
Explain how a series of chapters, scenes,
or stanzas fits together to provide the overall
structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

80761EED9CCA4A9FA228EBF881523249.description:
Determine the meaning of words and
phrases as they are used in a text, including
figurative language such as metaphors and
similes.

9062748BA9BE41C4B07EDEB11CA7EB7A.description:
Compare and contrast two or more
characters, settings, or events in a story or
drama, drawing on specific details in the text
(e.g., how characters interact).

50A36B842D12423CA250BD06EC53A470.description:
Determine a theme of a story, drama, or
poem from details in the text, including how
characters in a story or drama respond to
challenges or how the speaker in a poem
reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.

222E16C6D89F494993A3741A6300C84F.description:
Quote accurately from a text when
explaining what the text says explicitly and
when drawing inferences from the text.

654DB0D110244C84B5B9BEC45D1C182F.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

E8CBBAF73C90416CA3D6905D9E8297A0.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research

34E785321AD64F679B85E34B0394ED44.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

E3D17E562C2C461BA8BE075384F7EEB1.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

2EBBB020EAFD4DEB8FA967E777D8EC7D.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

811FC9EF06924B9696D353CD82282E15.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

EE3D596BED7D40FBB9807AE7C6DDC418.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

CC4616700CBA4F60A821CA36A612D6E7.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience

6C482575B51F4D80B4195012D0C226C6.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

49D82A75071C4F638F28F4C874ABDA2D.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone

6955AF9AC18747718BC74328F8A3AA9E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic

83FC2DD1FE2B4C3CAEB29414F0FE5945.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

90F51D1391B54893ADBB64DF2EED0F55.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples

9DC7EA5FD5BA4EF996CA707B3B842B9D.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension

1AD2C4C919EA4B9BBC83AAE1CD642C32.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/ experiments, or technical processes.

821018EEC5564920A38FB9D52E9D87E6.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

22EF671100A04F6398E83EC9FAE9369C.description: Establish and maintain a formal style

A79A79452E3A4C7EA1EE5AF8EA69234E.description:
Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the
relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

1F8FEA6B1A1343A5842DED5AEC2BF7B9.description:
Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.
understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or
opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically

5230F4EA7EB649279ECDA8CD87DD787C.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

9E71FC2B93C84CEE877DCE99F7D18F2F.description:
By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the
grades 6-8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

2D8516B13362481DBB59393020669315.description:
Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same
topic.

0150889A01024C23B2DC0EFA694E5B6E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

3C328D09E91744E0A7C2DFCFE5773EA3.description:
Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps)

96ED762C06B04D258C4CD15451B7A424.description:
Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g.,

3596FF90A1324AE2A25920F3F4F3D77E.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including
vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

C64FE942F1C94D73A9BC86FFFA476BEB.description:
Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source;
provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

D506C42244EF4916A5D3CFC5C7D81EB9.description:
Cite specific textual evidence to
support analysis of primary and secondary
sources.

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Standards for English Language Arts Grades PreK - K

6FB772AC90E84769AA41473630DA8E73.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, being
read to, and responding to texts.

1DF50304F22A44A38CDE7382B3ED6BC8.description:

(e.g., note objects in the classroom that are small).

With modeling and support, demonstrate understanding of
frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their
opposites (antonyms).

With modeling and support, sort common objects into
categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the
categories represent.

With modeling and support from adults, explore word
relationships and nuances in word meanings.

9DF11DAF58E241368C3F6088C56B138E.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown words and phrases
based on pre-kindergarten reading and content.

handwriting.

convey meaning.

punctuation (e.g., period, question mark, exclamation point).

writing experiences.

Gain exposure to the most frequently occurring
prepositions (e.g. to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

me happy.)

slender, skinny, scrawny).

understanding of word relationships and nuances in
word meanings.

digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse,
housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple

3E40C0ECD519468B8D7B48D2BE5E47C8.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing,

080F79DE06024AF5922871CCE59FDFC7.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English

Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate

EECE5F57ADED464A9F695303FEA88FB4.description:
Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to

1021C640AFE043EEAEDED8DC964ABC82.description:

0007F9EA851A4FEEBE7CDD2A4C8D77A7.description:

ECBFCA1A5D034B319278B7BAE68E4FC7.description:

5F6A30FA0BE34828A839725D80809853.description:
Recall information from experiences or gather information from
provided sources to answer a question.

D667501881E044B8A5CD3FBFA9932EE7.description:
Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a

6A719558F8F143F38D977471CEC5E418.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

peers.

Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition

Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate

Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support

Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in

5F2ADE415C6D424CBF4C9B1B1BD91783.description:

Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to

document.title: Maryland College and Career Ready Standards for English language Arts Grades 6-8

8451B462C41D4ADAB46511B051BBF193.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade
appropriate general academic and domainspecific words and phrases; gather vocabulary
knowledge when considering a word or phrase
important to comprehension or expression.

AB9C4501026E490DBA0451D12C7A861E.description:
Distinguish among the
connotations (associations) of words with
similar denotations (definitions) (e.g.,
stingy, scrimping, economical, thrifty).

0E37447B8E0D4581A2D6DF9686C020EE.description:
Use the relationship between
particular words (e.g., cause/effect,
part/whole, item/category) to better
understand each of the words.

DA78003DF76C431194AB7E99A79748AE.description:
Interpret figures of speech (e.g.,
personification) in context.

3D8C7B6BF11A470B95E6545FF86224E5.description:
Demonstrate understanding of figurative
language, word relationships, and nuances in
word meanings.

A9F1CB8643914BA998D0A27C4AB99C8A.description:
Verify the preliminary
determination of the meaning of a word or
phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred
meaning in context or in a dictionary).

266E80C46D5B4CD486E7F4E42B9CE29D.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g.,
dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both
print and digital, to find the pronunciation
of a word or determine or clarify its
precise meaning or its part of speech.

0596D5D17DBC47D486B0F44654E8D056.description:
Use common, grade appropriate
Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to
the meaning of a word (e.g., audience,
auditory, audible).

4EA3B548C9DF49DF9DDAD97A0A5B58B4.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall
meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a
word's position or function in a sentence)
as a clue to the meaning of a word or
phrase.

06FBB93376EC44B79F3B0E23667EAECA.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of
unknown and multiple-meaning words and
phrases based on grade 6 reading and content,
choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5A7B99DC0FDF42C4925181CC27F13F17.description:
Maintain consistency in style and
tone. *

5DAAFCBCB832415DA8206C45AB80B692.description:
Vary sentence patterns for
meaning, reader/listener interest, and
style.*

62535E922D2345FD901F061EE3503A9B.description:
Use knowledge of language and its
conventions when writing, speaking, reading,
or listening.

11C564298E77406C92309B81842F32B5.description:
Use punctuation (commas,
parentheses, dashes) to set off
nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements. *

385BDD6CF6CB4B5CA1088AAB179F175D.description:
Demonstrate command of the
conventions of standard English capitalization,
punctuation, and spelling when writing.

96ABD04709744A31B57FE64BBFE5477E.description:
Recognize variations from
standard English in their own and others'
writing and speaking, and identify and use
strategies to improve expression in
conventional language. *

243E1677A1CD48B3BFB6C8560165A02A.description:
Recognize and correct vague
pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or
ambiguous antecedents).*

E3F79139E08141CA96D1A5727506BDB6.description:
Recognize and correct
inappropriate shifts in pronoun number
and person.*

F97D6704C1F44989BC3DAC34145F6F1F.description:
Ensure that pronouns are in the
proper case (subjective, objective,
possessive).

E7F14544C0904ED5AD7EF4D76BC3A786.description:
Demonstrate command of the
conventions of standard English grammar and
usage when writing or speaking.

0D0E535998F24235859818CFD8A6F80C.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts
and tasks, demonstrating command of formal
English when indicated or appropriate. (See
grade 6 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific
expectations.)

13C326661FCB414BAF19632CFF40D9B8.description:
Include multimedia components (e.g.,
graphics, images, music, sound) and visual
displays in presentations to clarify information.

88A1CCD68D93494D83F7D8F3D88C5C33.description:
Present claims and findings, sequencing
ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions,
facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or
themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate
volume, and clear pronunciation.

3C4A46E7A3FC4157829A2CB9B08B7696.description:
Delineate a speaker's argument and
specific claims, distinguishing claims that are
supported by reasons and evidence from
claims that are not.

CB72D02E536A45C285A92D685F364DCB.description:
Interpret information presented in
diverse media and formats (e.g., visually,
quantitatively, orally) and explain how it
contributes to a topic, text, or issue under
study.

6DE99FB696C94DB094159A439E84E192.description:
Review the key ideas expressed
and demonstrate understanding of
multiple perspectives through reflection
and paraphrasing.

2847D651B09F465FB34D9D0F5451D387.description:
Pose and respond to specific
questions with elaboration and detail by
making comments that contribute to the
topic, text, or issue under discussion.

236B3357F29346599FBE2A178B98FA93.description:
Follow rules for collegial
discussions, set specific goals and
deadlines, and define individual roles as
needed.

9F1B9C71566141A9A657431FBC4E56F2.description:
Come to discussions prepared,
having read or studied required material;
explicitly draw on that preparation by
referring to evidence on the topic, text, or
issue to probe and reflect on ideas under
discussion.

6FCD20B3CF73433D900178745EDF0181.description:
Engage effectively in a range of
collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in
groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners
on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on
others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

D475CD9EB8D04A8BB7581A9E11390629.description:
Write routinely over extended time
frames (time for research, reflection, and
revision) and shorter time frames (a single
sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

CB6F77DBB25C4767B2776D1FEC6E41D6.description:
Apply grade 6 Reading standards
to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Trace and
evaluate the argument and specific claims
in a text, distinguishing claims that are
supported by reasons and evidence from
claims that are not").

1F84646C1A93413E8675936EC1A0BB81.description:
Apply grade 6 Reading standards
to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast
texts in different forms or genres [e.g.,
stories and poems; historical novels and
fantasy stories] in terms of their
approaches to similar themes and topics").

F126780389B64BA58BACD415C03C0A7E.description:
Draw evidence from literary or
informational texts to support analysis,
reflection, and research.

3C32F54BF72F4C92B36B236FAD93EA3D.description:

multiple print and digital sources; assess the
credibility of each source; and quote or
paraphrase the data and conclusions of others
while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic
bibliographic information for sources.

08B492B9F22C45E4B55346BC738082B8.description:
Conduct short research projects to
answer a question, drawing on several sources
and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.
